Any Bid submitted after the deadline will not be accepted. Each Bidder will receive an email acknowledgment for each Bid submitted.
Independent Evaluator.
Purpose and Role of IE. GPC is utilizing the IE to oversee this All-Source RFP and to serve as the point of contact for all Participants. As provided in the RFP Rule, the IE serves to maintain fairness, transparency, and consistency in the RFP Process, which helps to prevent claims of favoritism in the evaluation and advancement of Submissions. Commission Rules require GPC to retain an IE, who is selected by and reports to the Commission in carrying out its duties and assisting with development of this All-Source RFP and evaluation of Submissions. 
The IE Website. The IE Website serves as the required forum for all RFP communication among the Evaluation Team, Participants, and all interested Persons. Any Participant or interested Person may only communicate with GPC, the IE, or Staff regarding this All-Source RFP through the IE Website. If any Participant or interested Person directs to Staff or GPC questions regarding any RFP information, Staff or GPC, as applicable, will direct the Participant or interested Person to the IE Website to ensure all communications are documented and treated consistently, fairly, and transparently. If a Participant attempts to make contact outside the process described in this All-Source RFP, Participant will be directed to the IE Website for all information and communication and will be reported to the IE for a violation of this All-Source RFP requirement. Repeated violation of this requirement may result in the Participant being prohibited from participating and Participant’s Submission(s) being disqualified. 
Standards of Conduct.
Standards of Conduct Regarding Affiliate Bids. GPC Affiliates may submit Bids in response to this All-Source RFP. Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(d) incorporates measures to segregate the Evaluation Team and any Affiliate Bid Team. The lists identifying the Evaluation Team and, if applicable, Affiliate Bid Team members are found on the Commission’s website under Docket No. 56368 and on the “Documents” page of the IE Website. Each Participant is encouraged to review these lists. Except when communication is facilitated by Staff and monitored by the IE, each Bidder is prohibited from discussing this All-Source RFP and any related documents with the Evaluation Team. GPC implemented specific controls to ensure RFP-related information is confined to the appropriate team. Additionally, before receipt of Bids, GPC, Staff, and the IE will implement procedural steps to ensure that all Bids from Affiliate Bid Teams and from non-Affiliates are evaluated using a common methodology applied in a manner that ensures that any Affiliate Bid does not receive any advantage in the evaluation. In all instances, an Affiliate Bid Team will be treated as a third-party Bidder.
Standards of Conduct for Company-Owned Proposals Submitted by the Company-Owned Proposal Team. To meet its identified capacity needs, GPC may develop and submit one or more Company-Owned Proposals in response to this All-Source RFP for Facilities that would be owned and operated by GPC. GPC must submit any Company-Owned Proposal through the IE Website by the date shown in the Solicitation Schedule. Company-Owned Proposals may include partnership arrangements or agreements between GPC and third parties or contractors that may collaborate to submit a joint proposal.
GPC Contractors. To ensure fairness to all Participants, the COP Team will not share with a GPC Contractor, or potential GPC Contractor, any non-public information about the RFP Process. No GPC Contractor or GPC Contractor Affiliate is allowed to submit a Bid in this All-Source RFP for the same Facility submitted in any Company-Owned Proposal. 
GPC Internal Communications. While not required under Commission Rules, GPC voluntarily imposes the Affiliate communications restrictions set out in Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3) to restrict communications between the Evaluation Team and the COP Team, except as noted regarding Specialized Technical Support Personnel in Section 1.3.2.C (Company-Owned Proposal Team and Specialized Technical Support Personnel). No COP Team member may share with any Primary Evaluation Team member any Company-Owned Proposal information related to the costs or specific characteristics of any aspect of any Company-Owned Proposal or its proposed Facility, except for communications facilitated by the IE and Staff and necessary for evaluation of a Company-Owned Proposal. In addition to the requirements of Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(d) establishing standards of conduct regarding any Evaluation Team member and any Affiliate Bid Team member, no COP Team member will be a member of any Affiliate Bid Team nor communicate with any Affiliate Bid Team member in violation of Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(d). GPC will not tolerate conduct or communication regarding the development of any Company-Owned Proposal by the COP Team that would unfairly influence the design or evaluation processes for this All-Source RFP. 
Company-Owned Proposal Team and Specialized Technical Support Personnel. The COP Team will develop any Company-Owned Proposal in a manner that preserves the integrity and fairness of the RFP Process for all Participants. Due to their functional expertise and breadth of job responsibilities, Specialized Technical Support Personnel may be involved both with development of a Company-Owned Proposal and with certain aspects of this All-Source RFP. The RFP information provided to Specialized Technical Support Personnel is limited to the scope of their job responsibilities. Specialized Technical Support Personnel serving as members of both the Evaluation Team and the COP Team will not be allowed to determine the total economic benefit of Submissions. GPC will not substitute any dual-role Specialized Technical Support Personnel without first consulting Staff and the IE.
Development of this All-Source RFP.
Draft RFP Documents. Consistent with Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(e), GPC prepared the initial draft of this All-Source RFP with the consultation and input of Staff and the IE. The draft RFP Documents were posted to the IE Website by the date shown in the Solicitation Schedule.
Comment Period. The Solicitation Schedule provides the dates and duration of the Comment Period. Any Participant or interested Person desiring to submit written comments on any aspect of this All-Source RFP did so through the IE Website. If any Person commented about or offered a substantive change to the RFP Documents, the commenter was prompted to provide a mark-up of the applicable section showing its proposed changes, along with the rationale for the suggested change, for GPC’s consideration. The Evaluation Team, Staff, and IE reviewed all comments received. After the Comment Period, the Evaluation Team aggregated common themes from the comments received and provided responses to the IE for posting on the IE Website for the benefit of all Participants and interested Persons.
Bidders’ Conference. The Bidders’ Conference was held in-person and virtually on the date shown in the Solicitation Schedule. Any potential Participant or interested Person was given the opportunity during the Bidders’ Conference to ask questions concerning the RFP Process and the draft RFP Documents with GPC, Staff, and IE. Any Participant or interested party registered for the Bidders’ Conference on the IE Website. A recording of the Bidders’ Conference, the presentation materials, and written responses to all questions submitted during the Bidders’ Conference were posted on the IE Website after the Bidders’ Conference.
Frequently Asked Questions; Question and Answers. There is a tab on the IE Website for frequently asked questions (“FAQ”). Each Participant should review the FAQ before submitting a question on the IE Website because the question may be addressed in the FAQ. Throughout the RFP Process, a Participant may submit questions via the Question and Answer (“Q&A”) tab on the IE Website. When a Participant submits a question via the Q&A portal, the identity of the Participant asking the question is known to the IE and Staff only. After review by GPC, Staff, and the IE, the Q&A and FAQ documents are made publicly available to every Participant and interested Person.  
Conflicts. After the Commission approves this All-Source RFP, terms and conditions included in the final RFP Documents will supersede conflicting information, if any, included in the FAQ or Q&A.
Final RFP Documents Filed for Commission Approval. In accordance with the Solicitation Schedule, GPC publicly filed for Commission approval the proposed final versions of the RFP Documents. After approval by the Commission: (i) all registered users of the IE Website will be notified by email of the approval; (ii) a copy of the Bid Form and a list of required documents will be posted on the Documents page of the IE Website; and (iii) the final, approved version of the RFP Documents will be posted to the Commission’s website under Docket No. 56368 and the IE Website. 
PRODUCTS AND RESOURCES SOUGHT IN THIS All-Source RFP
Products Sought.
GPC seeks offers to sell capacity, including Ancillary Services, energy, if applicable, and all other Facility attributes, from Capacity Resources. Subject to Section 2.1.1 (Other Technology), a Submission may offer any reliable Capacity Resource that can meet the firmness and dispatchability requirements of this All-Source RFP, including but not limited to: (i) Standalone ESS with grid charge capability and a minimum SDDD of four hours; (ii) ESS with Renewable Resource (new or existing), with grid charge capability and a minimum SDDD of four hours; and (iii) thermal generation (natural gas, oil-fired, etc.). 
Other Technology. Participant may request to offer a Capacity Resource comprised of a technology or resource that is not described in Section 2.1(i) – (iii) (Products Sought) (each, an “Other Technology”), including any: (i) demand-response technology; (ii) ESS that is not a BESS (e.g., compressed-air energy storage, long-duration energy storage); (iii) firm, dispatchable import capability delivered over a dedicated high-voltage direct current (HVDC) line; and (iv) alternative firm resources with low or zero carbon emissions. To request to submit an Other Technology, Participant must contact the IE and submit the Other Technology form through the IE Website by no later than the Other Technology proposal deadline set forth in the Solicitation Schedule. Upon request, Participant must provide information to the IE regarding the Other Technology. The IE will research and review Participant’s proposed Other Technology and discuss findings with Staff and the Evaluation Team. After the IE completes its research, review, and discussions, the IE will advise Participant whether a Submission utilizing Participant’s proposed Other Technology will be accepted as a Submission that meets the requirements of this All-Source RFP. GPC will not consider for this All-Source RFP non-dispatchable technologies, including: (i) third-party aggregators; or (ii) other demand response options that do not: (a) meet the minimum Facility Size parameters described in Section 3.2.1 (Facility Size Parameters) at each Site; or (b) allow firm control of the demand response technology and associated infrastructure solely by GPC via AGC.
Facility Ownership Structures. 
 Under this All-Source RFP, Participants may offer Submissions proposing one of two ownership structures for Facilities:
Seller-Owned Facilities. GPC will accept Bids for New Resources and Existing Resources where Seller will retain Facility ownership. The Awarded Contract that a Winning Bidder would execute would be a PPA, where GPC would have exclusive rights to the Facility’s capacity.
GPC-Owned Facilities. GPC will accept Bids for Existing Resources comprising Capacity Resources where Bidder proposes to transfer to GPC Facility ownership. The Awarded Contract that a Winning Bidder would execute would be an APA. GPC may submit a Company-Owned Proposal offering a New Resource.
Consideration of APA Bids. GPC will consider APA Bids for Capacity Resources that are interconnected to the STT, except that any ESS must interconnect to the Southern Company Transmission System. GPC will consider offers for partial ownership of or partial unit(s) of an Existing Resource that is a CC or CT.
APA Bid Requirements. A Bidder offering an APA Bid must submit the same forms as a PPA Bidder, but an APA Bidder must also complete additional questions on the APA questionnaire found in the Bid Form, which indicates the information GPC must receive to perform necessary due diligence.
APA Bid Evaluation. APA Bids will be evaluated alongside PPA Bids and Company-Owned Proposal(s). If an APA Bid advances to the Conforming List, the evaluation of the APA Bid requires additional due diligence as described in Exhibit A (Due Diligence Phases and Fees Overview (APA Bids Only)). 
Generating Resource and Business Entity Purchase. If an APA Bid advances to the Short List, and even though GPC is likely only interested in the purchase of the Facility itself, GPC may also consider purchasing the business entity that owns the Existing Resource, subject to reaching acceptable terms and conditions. GPC may ask the APA Bidder to submit an offer allowing GPC to purchase the business entity that holds the Existing Resource. If the APA Bidder chooses to offer the business entity for purchase, GPC will have the right to proceed with the purchase of either the Existing Resource or the Existing Resource together with the business entity. 
Winning Bid APA Execution. If an APA Bid advances as a winning Bid, APA execution will occur in accordance with the Solicitation Schedule. Bidder and GPC must agree on a transaction closing date as soon as practicable once the parties obtain the required regulatory approvals.
Bids for Existing Resources or New Resources.
 Under this All-Source RFP, Bidders may submit Bids for both Existing Resources and New Resources. The Awarded Contract for:
An Existing Resource would be in the form of either an APA or PPA, depending on whether GPC or Seller would be the ultimate owner of the Existing Resource; or
A New Resource that has not yet been constructed, but that would ultimately be owned by Seller, would be a PPA in the form of one of the pro forma PPAs. 
ESS Submissions.
 For ESS Submissions, GPC will consider a Facility structured as: (i) Standalone ESS with grid charging capability; or (ii) ESS with Renewable Resource, with grid charging capability. In addition to the subsections that immediately follow, the pro forma ESS with Renewable Resource PPA and pro forma ESS PPA provide the parameters for the acceptable and applicable use of an ESS under this All-Source RFP, including the performance metrics GPC will apply to measure ESS performance and determine any reduction to Monthly capacity payments. GPC’s evaluation of an ESS Submission in this RFP will be appropriately focused upon the capacity use of the ESS, as further described in Exhibit G (Overview of Evaluation Methodology), which is to ensure system reliability.
Degradation; Performance Metrics. GPC is not responsible for any degradation of any Facility over the PPA Term, whether because of GPC scheduling, charging, or discharging of energy. As set forth in the pro forma ESS PPAs, and as applicable to all generating types, the ESS is subject to Monthly and annual performance metrics and must maintain the guaranteed SDDC, guaranteed SDDD, and guaranteed RTE for the PPA Term. Bidders should carefully review the applicable pro forma PPA to become familiar with these performance metrics, as deficient performance will reduce the payment owed to Seller under the PPA.
Interconnection Requirements. Any Participant offering an ESS Submission must be familiar with, and must comply with, Southern Company Transmission’s Interconnection Requirements for Transmission Connected Inverter-Based Resources, which is available at https://www.oasis.oati.com/woa/docs/SOCO/SOCOdocs/SOCO_Inverter-Based-Gen_Interconnection-Technical-Requirements.pdf.
Standalone ESS. A Participant offering a Standalone ESS must provide: (i) a description of the ESS; (ii) if offering a PPA, the plan to maintain the ESS to ensure the ESS performs as evaluated for the PPA Term; (iii) the guaranteed SDDC (AC); (iv) an annual schedule of the guaranteed RTE for the PPA Term or Facility Design Life, as applicable; and (v) any other information required by the Bid Form. GPC must have the exclusive right, without penalty, to discharge and charge the ESS by dispatching it in accordance with Section 3.5.1 (AGC). To ensure GPC can toll grid charging energy, an ESS must interconnect to a substation owned by GPC on the Southern Company Transmission System, which means a Southern Company entity must be the Interconnection Provider. GPC will provide (toll) all energy required to charge a Standalone ESS not paired with a Renewable Resource, but Seller will be solely responsible for Station Service, including any Auxiliary Operational Load. 
ESS with Renewable Resource. A Participant may offer to pair an ESS with either an existing Renewable Resource or a new Renewable Resource to be constructed as part of the Facility. If Participant offers an existing Renewable Resource, the existing Renewable Resource must be: (a) under a power purchase agreement with GPC procured through a prior GPC RFP; (b) paired with an ESS and offered under the Pro Forma Power Purchase Agreement for Firm Capacity, Energy Storage Services, and Ancillary Services from a Battery Energy Storage System [Paired with a Renewable Resource] for 2026 All-Source Capacity Request for Proposals for Need Years 2032 –2033; or (c) if the Submission is a COP, owned by GPC. In addition to the information required by Section 2.4.3 (Standalone ESS), an ESS with Renewable Resource Submission must also include: (i) a description of the Renewable Resource (including the generation type of the Renewable Resource (e.g., solar panels, wind turbines)); (ii) the total expected Renewable Resource capacity (AC); and (iii) a Profile reflecting the Renewable Resource to demonstrate the charging contribution of the Renewable Resource.  
If Participant offers to pair an ESS with an existing Renewable Resource that is currently committed to GPC under a separate PPA, then the parties must amend the existing Renewable Resource PPA to accommodate and allow for the paired operation of the ESS and the Renewable Resource. Exhibit M (Renewable Resource PPA Amendment Overview) outlines the anticipated terms and conditions of the Renewable Resource PPA amendment.
KEY PROJECT REQUIREMENTS
PPA Term, Facility Design Life, RCOD, and RCD. 
PPA Term and Facility Design Life. GPC will consider Bids for: (i) PPAs with a PPA Term of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, or 30 Annual Periods, at Bidder’s option; and (ii) APAs for Facilities with a Facility Design Life of at least 10 years. 
RCOD and RCD. GPC seeks and will give preference to Capacity Resources with Delivery Commencement Dates no later than November 30, 2032. However, Participant may offer a Capacity Resource with a Delivery Commencement Date that is earlier or later than the identified need years, and GPC will evaluate if the Submission is an economical option that meets customer needs. Participant offering a Facility comprised of multiple units may propose separate in-service dates for each unit so long as Participant guarantees each in-service date. Each Participant must indicate the RCOD, RCD, or DCD, as applicable, in its Submission.
 GPC may decline to enter into a PPA or APA with any Bidder if, in GPC’s opinion, in consultation with the IE and Staff, the transmission facilities cannot be constructed in time to achieve Commercial Operation or Closing by the applicable in-service date set forth in the Solicitation Schedule. Bidders may consult the Southern Companies’ Seller Interconnection Business Practices document posted on OASIS for information related to interconnection activity timeframes and limitations. If Seller fails to achieve Commercial Operation or Closing by the RCOD or RCD, as applicable, Seller must pay Delay Damages to GPC under the Awarded Contract. Delay Damages will be calculated in accordance with Section 2 (Delay Liquidated Damages)  in Exhibit D (Summary of Fees, Costs, Security, and Deadlines), Attachment 1 (Performance Security and Liquidated Damages Summary).
Facility Size and Output.
Facility Size Parameters. Except for any Uprate Submission, Partial Output Bid, and QF participating in this All-Source RFP under Part 9 (Qualifying Facilities), the offered Contracted Capacity or proposed Facility under an APA must be at least 50 MW. Each proposed Facility, including any Uprate Submission, must not exceed 1,550 MW. However, GPC reserves the right to release any Submission offering a Facility sized larger than the Southern Company Most Severe Single Contingency (MSSC) value (1,300 MW) based on potential unique reliability constraints or adverse cost impacts. If a Submission offers multiple units located on the same Site, each unit may be sized less than 50 MW so long as, when combined, the Facility size is at least 50 MW and all units deliver to the same Point of Delivery. A Participant cannot offer multiple units to be located on different Sites. If Participant offers multiple units in a single Submission, the Submission must indicate the size of each unit and whether each unit may advance separately at the pricing stated in the Submission, including the dollar per kilowatt ($/kW) annual capacity price stated in the Submission. The Submission must clearly state if units can or cannot advance separately or in combinations. If Participant desires to offer different pricing for different unit combinations, the Submission must specifically identify this pricing. 
ESS Submissions. Except for an Uprate Submission, a proposed ESS must have an SDDC of at least 50 MW at the POI. Each ESS must have a minimum SDDD of at least four hours. The SDDC must be no more than 500 MW at the POI. An ESS must have grid charging capability.    
Partial Output and Incremental Capacity Bids.  
Existing Resources. Except as provided in this Section 3.2.2.A (Existing Resources), each Bid for an Existing Resource must offer 100% ownership of, or entitlement to, the full Nominal Capability of the Existing Resource.
CC/CT. For CC and CT Existing Resources, GPC will consider any Uprate Submission, Partial Output Bid, and APA Bid offering partial ownership of the Capacity Resource. 
ESS. For ESS Existing Resources, GPC will consider any Uprate Submission and PPA Bid for a Modular BESS Facility meeting the requirements of Section 3.2.3 (Modular BESS Facility Submissions). 
Uprate Submissions and Partial Output Bids. Any Uprate Submission may offer less than 50 MW. Any Partial Output Bid: (a) may offer an initial Contracted Capacity less than 50 MW, so long as the Contracted Capacity increases to at least 50 MW during the PPA Term; and (b) must offer GPC first call rights to the Contracted Capacity, which means GPC must receive exclusive rights to call upon the Contracted Capacity and receive all associated energy without regard to any other offtaker. Participants who intend to offer an Uprate Submission or Partial Output Bid must review and comply with the Uprate and Partial Output Bid Guidance document available on the IE Website.
New Resources. For any New Resource that is not a Modular BESS Facility, each Bid must offer 100% entitlement to the full capability of the Capacity Resource.
Modular BESS Facility Submissions. GPC will accept Submissions that offer capacity from one or more BESS blocks comprising a Modular BESS Facility if the Submission meets the requirements of this Section 3.2.3 (Modular BESS Facility Submissions). For clarity, a Modular BESS Facility is a single “generating facility” from a transmission interconnection perspective (including at the POI), but the Facility includes internal segmentation that supports independent operation of one or more BESS blocks. To be an eligible Submission, a Submission offering one or more, but not all, blocks of a Modular BESS Facility must be capable of operating as a standalone BESS consistent with all RFP requirements, including those concerning availability, dispatchability, and any other performance guarantee. If GPC determines that shared infrastructure, controls, or operational dependencies could impair GPC’s ability to utilize the offered BESS as a capacity resource in accordance with RFP requirements, GPC will not advance the Submission for further consideration. If a Bid offering one or more, but not all, blocks of a Modular BESS Facility advances to the Short List, GPC will revise the pro forma PPA to implement the requirements of this Section 3.2.3 as a Facility-specific modification.
Independent Operation. The BESS block(s) offered to GPC must be exclusively committed to GPC (e.g., not used to serve any other offtaker) and capable of independent operation such that GPC can fully exercise its dispatch and grid charging rights without reliance on, or impairment by, the operation of any other block of the Modular BESS Facility that is not committed to GPC. To be capable of independent operation, the offered BESS block(s) must include: (i) an independent plant controller; (ii) an independent AGC system; and (iii) independent metering, data telemetry, and other data reporting, including independent data sufficient to confirm compliance with the Georgia Territorial Act and any other applicable law. GPC must have the right to review and approve the proposed metering, telemetry, and AGC configurations for the entire Modular BESS Facility. 
 POI and Other Considerations. Bidder is solely responsible for: (i) ensuring Facility design, interconnection facilities, and internal configuration are sufficient to support the operational requirements of all BESS blocks, including those committed to GPC and any other offtaker; (ii) ensuring that Facility-level constraints do not impact guaranteed BESS performance; and (iii) assuming the risk of transmission-level reliability adjustments, curtailments, or other operational limitations imposed by the transmission provider at the POI that impact one or more BESS blocks, including those impacting Facility availability and dispatchability under the PPA that may lead to monthly capacity payment reductions.
Acceptable Interconnection Design Configurations. Part 6 (Modular BESS Facility Interconnection Design Configurations) of Exhibit B (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements) includes two acceptable Seller-side interconnection design configurations for a Modular BESS Facility where one or more, but not all, BESS blocks are committed to GPC (i.e., GPC does not receive 100% of the Modular BESS Facility’s capacity under the PPA). GPC prefers, especially when multiple entities offtake from a Modular BESS Facility, that the portion of the Modular BESS Facility committed to GPC be interconnected by an independent generation tie line that will not be used by or for any other offtaker, as shown as Option A in Part 6 of Exhibit B.
GPC Consent Required for Facility Changes. A Winning Bidder must obtain GPC’s written consent before making any material change to Facility design, performance, or output (as specified in the Bid and considered by GPC in Bid evaluation).
Location of Facilities.
Facility Location. Except for ESS Submissions, GPC will accept Submissions for a Facility located within or outside of the STT, so long as the Facility: (i) can deliver energy to GPC in accordance with one of the interconnection options set forth in Exhibit B (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements); and (ii) otherwise meets RFP requirements, including AGC capability. Any ESS Facility must interconnect to the Southern Company Transmission System (i.e., a Southern Company entity must be the Interconnection Provider). A Bidder may not submit a Bid that locates the Facility on GPC property. Only a Company-Owned Proposal may propose a Facility on GPC property.
ESS with Renewable Resource Location. Any ESS paired with a Renewable Resource Submission must interconnect to the same POI as the Renewable Resource.
New Resources.
 Each Participant proposing a New Resource must propose a specific POI for its Facility. GPC (through the IE) may suggest a different POI (regarding location or voltage) if it would result in more favorable economic consideration of the Submission. Participant will be responsible for all equipment necessary to interconnect the Facility to the Interconnection Facilities at the POI. All transmission facilities beyond the proposed POI (into the network transmission grid) will be owned by the Transmission Service Provider.
Technical Pre-Screen. In furtherance of GPC’s commitment to an efficient evaluation process, GPC will release a technical pre-screen form. GPC strongly encourages Participants to provide the specified technical data about their project(s) before the Bid Period opens. The data collected will be validated by GPC’s transmission evaluation team to help ensure each Submission is properly structured and ready for evaluation. 
2026 Annual Cluster Study. For each Submission offering a New Resource that will interconnect to the Southern Company Transmission System, but excluding any New Resource eligible for Surplus Interconnection Service, Participant must have an existing IA or  have entered the 2025 or 2026 Annual Cluster Study.
Dispatchability.
 Capacity Resources offered in this All-Source RFP must be fully dispatchable and available to meet GPC’s scheduling instructions for the PPA Term or Facility Design Life, as applicable, which means the Facility can flexibly adjust its output in response to GPC’s scheduling instructions, subject to any technical limit or other requirement stated in the Awarded Contract. GPC may give preference to Submissions that offer a Facility that can be scheduled on shorter notice  and that has greater operational flexibility.
AGC. Because of their expected use and cost-effectiveness, each Capacity Resource offered through a Bid for full output of the Capacity Resource must be capable of operating on AGC throughout the PPA Term or Facility Design Life, as applicable, including any Renewable Resource offered as part of an ESS Submission. Seller will be responsible for conforming to GPC’s requirements to integrate AGC functionality and for all costs to make the Facility respond to GPC’s AGC signals. For any Partial Output Bid, the Facility must either be capable of operating on AGC or, if AGC capability is not provided, must comply with GPC’s dispatch and scheduling instructions. In each case, GPC will have the right, but not the obligation, to dispatch the Facility in the AGC mode. Each Bid must include the cost of the operation in its pricing. For PPA Bids involving Facilities that are not connected to the STT, Bidders should verify dynamic transfer capability and protocols with the Southern Company Transmission System to ensure proper telemetry communications in accordance with the Southern OATT. 
Availability.
 GPC will rely, in part, on the Contracted Capacity and energy, where applicable, supplied under a PPA to provide dependable and reliable electric service to meet the needs of its customers. Accordingly, GPC will require stringent protection for GPC and its customers against Seller failures to deliver Contracted Capacity and energy in accordance with the PPA.
Guaranteed Availability. Any PPA will contain provisions that require Seller to forfeit a portion of the capacity payment as compensation to GPC for damages GPC will incur because of Facility availability below 96%. After taking scheduled maintenance outages and Alternate Resource delivery, if applicable, into account, availability during any Monthly period that is below 60% will result in a 100% forfeiture of the Monthly capacity payment. Bidder may review the applicable pro forma PPA for more information regarding the availability calculation and adjustments to the capacity payment (which may be determined by replacement costs). In addition, a PPA Event of Default will occur if Facility availability remains below 60% for a certain extended period as specified in the PPA. 
Multiple Modes of Operation.
 For a PPA Bid offering a Facility with multiple modes of operation, Bidder must specify the guaranteed nominal capacity of each mode and quote a single capacity Bid price for the entire output of the Facility. If during any Annual Period the capacities designated by mode are different from their respective guaranteed nominal capabilities by mode, an adjustment to the capacity payment will be made in a manner that reflects the value of each mode to GPC. The adjustment is described, for example, in Exhibit B (Capacity; Capacity Payments and Payment Reductions; Buydown) of the pro forma CC PPA. If during any Annual Period the capacities designated by mode match their respective guaranteed nominal capabilities by mode, the capacity payment will match the single capacity Bid price. 
APA Bids. For an APA Bid with multiple modes of operation, a Bidder must provide the expected nominal capacity output for each mode.
Firmness of Proposed Resources.
 To be considered responsive, a Submission must demonstrate an appropriate level of firmness, which means the Facility must deliver capacity for the duration of any period of guaranteed commitment in accordance with GPC’s scheduling instructions, even under adverse conditions (i.e., operating or system conditions that may limit or challenge Facility performance but that are not excused by a Force Majeure Event (as defined in the Awarded Contract), including foreseeable weather variability, routine operating stresses, and other expected or reasonably foreseeable system conditions). GPC’s evaluation will assess the reliability and economic value of limits indicated in the Submission. Each Submission must propose to provide the proposed capacity and energy, if applicable, to GPC from specific, dedicated resource(s) on an unencumbered, first-call basis and priority. 
Demineralization.
 The use of demineralized water supply for a resource should not limit the operations or delivery of capacity. CCs operating on natural gas should be able to support at least 24 hours of full load generation plus peaking or secondary modes of operation. Demineralized water intended for use in conjunction with fuel oil operation should match the specified storage capacity for fuel oil in Section 3.10 (Fuel/Energy Plan). Bidder must also have adequate demineralized water replenishment capabilities at the Facility.
Fuel/Energy Plan.
 For evaluation purposes, GPC will develop an individual fuel plan for each CC and CT Submission and a grid charging plan for any ESS Submission to reliably and economically meet the fuel/energy supply requirements for those Submissions. The projected fuel/energy plans will be developed in a consistent and fair manner for all Submissions.
Fuel Evaluation.
 Natural gas prices will be linked to a single Monthly forecast of gas prices at a common point (Henry Hub). Delivered gas prices will include applicable gas transportation charges, fuel retention rates, historical basis differentials, and taxes. GPC will evaluate fuel-related requirements, including the purchase of firm gas transportation and storage, as follows.
CT.
 GPC prefers that CTs have dual-fuel capability to burn natural gas and oil. Participant may propose alternative secondary fuel in its Submission (e.g., hydrogen blend). Gas storage will be evaluated consistent with other GPC CT units, and fuel oil inventory costs will be applied as appropriate. The Submission must indicate the permitted hours of operation and the maximum hours per year the Facility is permitted to run on fuel oil. The supporting facilities (including infrastructure and property interests) and operation for onsite fuel oil storage, if applicable, must comply with the following standards:
CT Facilities with sufficient fuel oil backup will not require firm gas transportation provided the oil can be burned year-round. If a CT Facility has sufficient fuel oil backup but cannot burn oil in the summer Months, then, for Months with seasonal limitations on oil, the Submission must include five to twelve hours firm transportation per Day on gas depending on site limitations and unit heat rate. 
For an existing CT Facility with dual-fuel capability, the Facility should include: (1) sufficient fuel oil storage to operate the Facility for 24 continuous hours, without replenishment, at full load; and (2) adequate replenishment capabilities. 
For a new-build or transfer CT Facility with dual-fuel capability, the Facility must include: (1) sufficient fuel oil storage capacity to operate the Facility for 72 continuous hours, without replenishment, at full load; and (2) adequate replenishment capabilities.
Unless otherwise mutually agreed by GPC and Seller under a PPA, Seller will acquire, permit, construct, own, operate, and maintain all facilities, infrastructure, auxiliary systems (e.g., water system), and property interests necessary to ensure sufficient fuel oil storage capacity and reliable replenishment capability as required to operate the Facility. If a Participant offering a CT Facility cannot meet the storage and replenishment capabilities outlined above, Participant must indicate its storage and replenishment capabilities. GPC will evaluate this as a qualitative, non-price factor. 
GPC and Seller will develop additional Site-specific requirements and objectives necessary to implement the foregoing standards as a part of the Awarded Contract.
CC. Each CC Facility will be evaluated with sufficient firm gas transportation to allow 24 hours of operation at full load plus peaking or secondary modes of operation. In each CC Submission, Participant must indicate the permitted hours of operation. 
Fuel Tolling for CC and CT PPA Bids.
 Each PPA Bidder offering a CT or CC Facility must submit a firm fuel transportation proposal to confirm that the resource can meet the firmness requirements of this RFP for the PPA Term, but Bidders are not required to have a firm fuel transportation arrangement in effect at the time of Bid submission. 
Tolling. Except for Partial Output Bids, GPC requires a fuel tolling arrangement (i.e., an arrangement in which GPC is responsible for fuel supply and transportation) for CC and CT Facilities for which the Bidder does not have a pre-existing fuel transportation arrangement. Seller under the PPA will be responsible for fuel for any Facility offered through a Partial Output Bid.
Preexisting Fuel Arrangements. Regarding resources for which the Bidder has a pre-existing fuel transportation arrangement, GPC prefers a fuel tolling arrangement with assignment/release of the pre-existing fuel transportation arrangement. If a fuel tolling arrangement with assignment/release of the pre-existing fuel transportation arrangement is proposed, this will be factored into the evaluation. Bidder must provide specific data regarding the costs and rates that will be assigned/released in accordance with the fuel transportation arrangement as a Bid term.
GPC Delivery of Gas. Under a fuel tolling arrangement, GPC will be responsible for delivering to the agreed-upon gas delivery point sufficient quantities of natural gas to generate energy in accordance with GPC’s energy schedules. GPC will bear the risk of loss of natural gas until it is delivered to the delivery point. The party responsible for causing any imbalance will be responsible for payment of any imbalance charges assessed by the pipeline operator.
Charging Plan for ESS Bids.
 GPC requires each ESS to connect to the Southern Company Transmission System. Each ESS PPA must allow GPC to charge the ESS from the Southern Company Transmission System and to dispatch all energy stored in the ESS. In addition to grid charging, an ESS with Renewable Resource is expected to be appropriately sized to allow the Renewable Resource to be the primary source of charging for the ESS.
Alternate Delivery.
 If a CT or CC Facility is physically unable to meet GPC’s schedules, and to avoid a commensurate reduction in the calculated availability of the Facility, an Awarded Contract will contain provisions that give Seller the option to elect a physical alternate delivery option for the duration of a Facility outage or derate. Alternate delivery does not apply to ESS Bids. The pro forma CC and CT PPAs provide examples of these alternate delivery rights.
Technical Requirements.
 All Facilities must comply with NERC EOP-012-3 (Extreme Cold Weather Preparedness and Operations) and any applicable successor reliability standard. Exhibit L (Facility Technical Requirements) contains a general overview of the technical requirements with which each New Resource must comply, as applicable.
Station Service; Retail Electric Service.
 Each Seller under an Awarded Contract is responsible for all Station Service at Seller’s expense. If the Facility is located in Georgia, Seller must arrange retail electric service for the Facility in accordance with the Georgia Territorial Electric Service Act. Seller must purchase Station Service provided by the local electric service provider (which may or may not be GPC) as necessary.
Environmental Compliance.
 All Submissions that advance to the Conforming List will undergo a comprehensive environmental review to ensure compliance with the requirements of this All-Source RFP, including the requirements found in the Environmental Assurances Guidance Document. Participant must cooperate with GPC’s Environmental Affairs Department, at Participant’s cost, regarding the environmental and cultural resources assessments, surveys, and studies performed for the Site, and for the property on which the Interconnection Facilities will be located, as well as any related Access Route. 
Site Assessment.
 Each Participant must conduct an Environmental Site Assessment that, at a minimum, considers the factors described in the Environmental Assurances Guidance Document.
Environmental Assurances Compliance Affidavit; Environmental Assurances.
 Each Participant must submit a notarized Environmental Assurances Compliance Affidavit, found in Exhibit K (Environmental Assurances Compliance Affidavit Form) that affirms Participant understands all environmental impacts and factors related to the Project and, at a minimum, agrees to fully consider the environmental requirements of this RFP to avoid, minimize, and if necessary, permit and mitigate the Project’s environmental impacts. If a Submission advances to the Conforming List, it will undergo a comprehensive review to ensure Participant complied with the environmental compliance requirements of this RFP. Furthermore, Participant must submit Environmental Assurances documentation to GPC by the deadline stated in the Solicitation Schedule. If Participant does not provide sufficient and acceptable documentation supporting the Environmental Assurances, as described in the Environmental Assurances Guidance Document, the Submission may be moved to the Release List.
Gas-Fired Requirements. 
NOx and SO2 Allowances. Seller, under a gas-fired resource PPA, will be required to use for GPC’s benefit all NOx Allowances and SO2 Allowances that are allocated to or for the Facility, or that are otherwise granted to Seller for the Facility, by any Governmental Authority or under any applicable law or Consent, including through any state or federal set-aside program, for the calendar years covered, in whole or in part, by the Annual Periods. If NOx emissions or SO2 emissions from the Facility resulting from energy generated to meet GPC’s scheduling instructions exceed the NOx Allowances or SO2 Allowances that are required to be supplied and used by Seller, GPC will be responsible for supplying only the additional NOx Allowances or SO2 Allowances. GPC’s responsibility to provide any additional allowance will be capped at the emissions rates (per state and per MWh of energy) proposed by the Participant. During Bid evaluation, GPC will calculate emissions utilizing Bidder’s proposed rates and GPC’s anticipated scheduling of the Facility. Complete details of these obligations are described in the pro forma CC and CT PPAs.
Greenhouse Gas Compliance. Each Bidder proposing a gas-fired Capacity Resource must supply a narrative description of Bidder’s proposed plan for complying with any regulation designed to avoid, reduce, utilize, or sequester air pollutants or greenhouse gases.
CC Operating Flexibility. 
 A Participant offering a 2-on-1 CC Facility must offer operation in the 1-on-1 mode if technically feasible by design. Operating in 1-on-1 mode entails the ability to operate a single CT, one HRSG, and the steam turbine while second CT is shutoff. A Participant offering this type of Facility must offer cycling from 2-on-1 operation down to 1-on-1 mode and back up to 2-on-1 mode if technically feasible by design. A Participant may also propose a 1-on-1 CC Facility.
Operation Mode Pricing. 
 A Participant offering a 2-on-1 CC Facility should offer 1-on-1 operation pricing based on the cost of operating in this mode. This should entail a start charge that accurately represents the cost of starting the Facility in the 1-on-1 mode and the cost of moving from 1-on-1 mode to 2-on-1 mode. The Participant should also provide heat rate curves consistent with the actual cost of 1-on-1 operation. If a Participant proposes a resource with other operational capabilities, (e.g., 3-on-1 or power augmentation), Participant’s Submission must offer the operational flexibility consistent with the Facility capabilities and pricing based on the cost of providing such operational flexibility. 
Compliance with Laws Generally.
 It is Participant’s sole responsibility to take all necessary actions to satisfy any regulatory requirements, licenses, and permits that may be imposed on Participant by any federal, state, or local Governmental Authority concerning the permitting, development, construction, operation, maintenance, addition, renewal, retirement, or disposal of the Facility, or concerning the generation, storage, sale, or delivery of energy. GPC will cooperate with Winning Bidder(s) to provide information or other assistance as may reasonably be requested by the Bidder to satisfy regulatory requirements. Bidder must likewise provide necessary information and assistance to GPC concerning GPC’s regulatory approvals.
PRICING, FEES, AND SECURITY
PPA Pricing.
 PPA Bid prices must include all costs GPC will pay for the capacity and any energy to be delivered under the PPA in accordance with GPC’s AGC setpoint signals or other scheduling instructions. GPC will not be responsible for any other cost associated with the Facility, including Station Service, fuel for testing, transmission system interconnection, and all costs (including fuel) incurred to accomplish synchronization. Monthly Capacity Payments to Seller under the PPA will be based upon: (i) SDDC for ESS; and (ii) Declared Standard Capacity (as defined in the applicable pro forma PPA) for a CT or CC. 
Escalating Pricing. A PPA Bidder may submit a Bid with the capacity payment escalated at a fixed percentage not to exceed 2.5% in any Annual Period. The minimum escalation during any Annual Period for the capacity payment will be limited to 0%. 
Variable Pricing (Not Applicable to ESS Bids). Any applicable energy pricing, Variable O&M, and heat rates must be quoted as indicated in the Bid Form. Variable O&M must escalate at actual GDPIPD per annum (pricing will be escalated starting on the DCD). Bidders are encouraged to propose variable costs consistent with their actual realized variable costs. The Bid heat rate should closely approximate the anticipated heat rate. If the Bid’s variable components are not consistent with Facility design specifications, GPC may request, through the IE, that Bidder modify its Bid(s). This cost-based pricing approach must reflect the following components, as applicable: (i) Variable O&M; (ii) start cost; (iii) heat rate; and (iv) fuel commodity cost. 
APA Pricing.
 Each APA Bid must provide an “all-in” price that includes all customary and reasonable facilities necessary for reliable operation of the Facility, including transmission interconnection, gas lateral, any other facilities, and the Site. An APA Facility must include the Facility’s major equipment and all auxiliary equipment and facilities necessary or used for the production, control, delivery, or monitoring of electricity produced on the property. All equipment and other facilities installed on the Facility’s side of the POI and the primary gas delivery point, if applicable, must be considered part of the Facility. All data required in the Bid Form, including capacity, heat rate, Variable O&M, startup fuel, and Facility availability must be based on testing, past performance, and good faith estimates for an APA Facility.
Option to Purchase Land. If an APA Bidder owns property adjacent to the Site, the Bidder may include within its Bid an offer to sell to GPC the adjacent property for an optional price stated in the Bid.
Due Diligence. Concurrent with GPC’s initial economic screening of all conforming Submissions, GPC will begin APA due diligence assessments as generally described in Exhibit A (Due Diligence Phases and Fees Overview (APA Bids Only)) to determine GPC’s best estimate of the cost to own and operate the Facility. 
Change of Law. 
 If a Change of Law occurs, Participant may request to adjust its Submission pricing if the quotient of: (i) Change of Law Expenditures; divided by (ii) the Facility’s Nominal Capability, exceeds $4/kW (“Threshold Amount”).
Notice. If Participant determines that any Change of Law will cause Change of Law Expenditures exceeding the Threshold Amount that are not accounted for in Participant’s Submission pricing, Participant must notify GPC through the IE Website no later than 15 Business Days after Participant knew or should have known of the Change of Law. Participant’s notice to GPC must identify in reasonable detail the claimed Change of Law and its likely effects on the Facility.  
Submissions Pricing Adjustment Request. For any eligible Change of Law that will cause Participant to incur Change of Law Expenditures exceeding the Threshold Amount and for which Participant provided timely notice in accordance with Section 4.3.1 (Notice), Participant may request approval to adjust its Submission pricing to account for Change of Law Expenditures. Participant must submit its request through the IE Website. Participant’s request must state Participant’s proposed Submission pricing adjustment and be supported by documentation sufficient for GPC to validate the need for and amount of Change of Law Expenditures. GPC will evaluate Participant’s request and reasonably determine if it is appropriate to allow Seller to adjust its Submission price by considering the requested adjustment amount, composition of the Competitive Tier, the Submission’s potential benefit to GPC customers, and any other quantitative or qualitative factor GPC deems appropriate. GPC will notify Participant of GPC’s determination through the IE Website. If a Change of Law will cause Participant to incur Change of Law Expenditures exceeding the Threshold Amount but GPC determines it will not agree to a pricing adjustment, GPC will notify Participant and allow Participant to withdraw its Submission without penalty (GPC will return Bid Security), at Participant’s election.
PPA Pricing Adjustments. If GPC agrees an adjustment is appropriate, GPC and Bidder will, each acting in a good faith and commercially reasonable manner and under the oversight of the IE and Staff, establish an appropriate annual fixed charge rate to apply to the original capital cost of the additions, modifications, or other capital expenditures that comprise Change of Law Expenditures for purposes of calculating an adjustment to the Annual Capacity Price(s) associated with capitalized additions or modifications to the Facility (determined in accordance with GAAP).  
APA and COP Pricing Adjustments. An APA Bidder or COP Team, as applicable, and GPC, each acting in a good faith and commercially reasonable manner under the oversight of the IE and Staff, will establish an adjustment to the in-service cost portion of Submission pricing to account for Change of Law Expenditures.
Pending Repeal of Carbon Capture Requirements. For purposes of this All-Source RFP, a Change of Law will be deemed to occur if the rule proposed by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency on June 11, 2025, to repeal the carbon capture, use, and sequestration requirements under 40 C.F.R. Part 60, Subpart TTTTa does not become legally effective on or before its stated effective date and, as a result, Participant must comply with additional carbon capture, use, and sequestration requirements.
Refreshed Submission Pricing. 
 GPC will use the “refreshed bid” process set out in Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(e)(ix), which allows a Participant to refresh its pricing. After the Conforming List is determined, the IE will contact each Participant with a Submission that advanced to the Conforming List to inform the Participant that it may better (increase or decrease) its Submission price as a final and best offer, as described in the applicable subsections below. The IE will post a ranking list on the IE Website showing each Participant’s relative rank. Each Participant on the Conforming List will be identified blindly, so each Participant may only see its rank compared to those of all other anonymous Submissions. GPC will further evaluate refreshed Submissions and advance a Competitive Tier in accordance with the RFP Rule and as described in Section 8.4 (Bid Lists).
Refreshed Submissions Process. Each Participant with a Submission advanced to the Conforming List may submit refreshed pricing (as limited by the subsections that follow) by the deadline stated in the Solicitation Schedule. Except as described in the subsections that follow, no changes to the Submission are allowed, including changes to Facility size, technology, or commercial operation date. Any refreshed Submission pricing will supersede the Submission’s initial price. At submission, Participant must also include a written narrative explaining why it is necessary for Participant to change its pricing. GPC will use Participant’s explanatory information for informational purposes and, to the extent the Submission is a winning Submission, in support of its Certification request. 
PPA Bid Refresh. Each PPA Bidder with a Bid that advances to the Conforming List will be given one opportunity to refresh the fixed-price portion of its Bid (i.e., capacity price and fuel transportation price). 
APA Bid Refresh. Each APA Bidder with a Bid that advances to the Conforming List will be given one opportunity to refresh its acquisition price.  
COP Refresh. If a COP advances to Conforming List, the COP Team will be given one opportunity to refresh the total in-service cost portion of the Company-Owned Proposal. 
Bid Fee.
 To help defray the cost of performing an evaluation of each Bid and the cost of retaining the IE pursuant to the RFP Rule, each Bidder must pay the Bid Fee for each Bid, except for Alternative Bids as described in Section 7.4 (Alternative Submissions; Multiple Submissions; Bid Fees). A portion of each Bid Fee in the amount of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) will be earmarked to offset IE costs. Bidder must pay the Bid Fee by 12:00 p.m. ET on the Bid Due Date.
Due Diligence Fees.
 To partially offset the cost of screening and assessments of an asset purchase, APA Bidders will be required to submit Due Diligence Fees as described in Exhibit A (Due Diligence Phases and Fees Overview (APA Bids Only)). The IE and Staff will review the allocation and accrual of costs involved in the assessments. A portion of Due Diligence Fees will be used to offset IE costs.
Winner’s Fee.
 As stated in Section 4.5 (Bid Fee) and Section 4.6 (Due Diligence Fees), portions of Bid Fees will be used to offset IE costs. The remainder of the IE cost will be covered by the Winner’s Fee. The Winner’s Fee will be determined after Commission Certification and once the final amount of Bid Fees, Due Diligence Fees, and IE cost is known, except in no event will the Winner’s Fee exceed one million dollars ($1,000,000.00) per Submission. The Winner’s Fee is calculated for each winning Submission, including any Company-Owned Proposal, as the pro rata share for any remaining IE or other RFP administration costs not covered by Bid Fees. If there are multiple winning Submissions, the remaining IE or other RFP administration costs will be allocated to winning Participant(s) on: (i) a MW-PPA Term basis for PPA(s); (ii) a MW-estimated-remaining-life basis for APA(s); and (iii) a MW-Facility Design Life basis for Company-Owned Proposals. Winning Bidder must pay the Winner’s Fee within 10 Days after receipt of notice of the final Winner’s Fee amount owed by Winning Bidder. If a Company-Owned Proposal advances to the Short List and is certified by the Commission as contemplated by Section 10.2 (Company-Owned Proposal Certification), GPC will be responsible for its Winner’s Fee. A Winning Bidder must pay its Winner’s Fee using the instructions included within GPC’s notice to Winning Bidder of the final Winner’s Fee amount.  
Bid Security.

 Any Bidder with a Bid that advances to the Conforming List must post Bid Security by no later than the deadline stated in the Solicitation Schedule. Bid Security is fully refundable to Bidder if: (i) GPC releases the Bid from consideration in this All-Source RFP for reasons other than Bidder non-compliance with RFP terms; or (ii) at the time Seller and GPC fully execute the Awarded Contract for the winning Bid. Bid Security is non-refundable if a Bidder withdraws its Bid at any time after posting Bid Security or otherwise fails to execute the pro forma PPA or APA after being advanced to the Short List. By submitting a Bid, Bidder acknowledges that GPC will be harmed if Bidder withdraws its Bid after advancing to the Conforming List and, as result, GPC will be entitled to retain Bid Security as liquidated damages, and not as a penalty, as the sole and exclusive remedy for Bidder’s failure or refusal to proceed in accordance with RFP terms.
Bid Security Amount. The Bid Security amount must equal $27/kW based on the Nominal Capability offered in the Bid. 
Bid Security for Alternative Bids and Mutually Exclusive Contingent Submissions. For Alternative Bids and mutually exclusive Contingent Submissions (i.e., only one of the Contingent Submissions can be accepted), Bidder may post a single Bid Security in an amount equal to the Bid Security amount required for the largest Alternative Bid or mutually exclusive Contingent Submission, as applicable. If Bidder withdraws any Alternative Bid or Contingent Submission, as applicable, the Bid Security will be forfeited, in its entirety, as described in this Section 4.8 (Bid Security). Following Bidder’s withdrawal, Bidder must immediately post a replacement Bid Security in the amount required for the next largest Alternative Bid for any remaining Alternative Bid.
Bids Offered in Multiple GPC RFPs. If Bidder is participating in a concurrent GPC RFP, except for any extended RFP period allowing customer-identified resource submissions, and offers the same Facility in both RFPs, Bidder may post a single Bid Security that secures both bids. Bid Security must equal the highest Bid Security required under the concurrent GPC RFPs. Bidder is solely responsible for taking any necessary action to ensure that Bid Security effectively secures its obligations under both RFPs, which may require Bidder to amend its Bid Security.
Pre-Approval of Bid Security. Each Bidder that intends to provide Bid Security in the form of a Surety Bond or a Letter of Credit must deliver a draft (unissued) Surety Bond or Letter of Credit for review and approval by GPC at Bid submission. Instructions for posting the draft and final Bid Security will be available on the IE Website. Pre-approved Bid Security submitted in the form of Surety Bond or Letter of Credit must be mailed via a reputable overnight courier to GPC at the following address:
Georgia Power Company C/O Southern Company Services Inc. Attention: Assistant Treasurer 
Bin No. SC140730 Ivan Allen Jr. Blvd.Atlanta, GA 30308
Bidder must upload a copy of Bid Security to the IE Website. Surety Bonds or Letters of Credit sent to any other address will be rejected. Bid Security in the form of cash must be submitted to GPC in accordance with the instructions posted on the IE Website.
Performance Security for Sellers.
 
PPA Performance Security. If a Seller is not Creditworthy, Seller must post and maintain Performance Security throughout the PPA Term. If Seller is Creditworthy, the credit terms of the PPA will be adjusted to reflect Seller’s Creditworthiness. 
PPA Performance Security Amount. PPA Performance Security will be calculated in accordance with the applicable Performance Security table in Exhibit D (Summary of Fees, Costs, Security, and Deadlines), Attachment 1 (Performance Security and Liquidated Damages Summary).
APA Performance Security Amount. Each Winning Bidder of an APA must, on or before execution of an APA, post and maintain Performance Security as required by the APA.
