Bid Preparation Costs.
 All costs related to preparation of any Bid in response to this All-Source RFP are the sole responsibility of Bidder. GPC will not reimburse or be held responsible for costs associated with any Bid prepared or submitted in response to this All-Source RFP. 
COMMUNICATION
Monitored Communications.
 Before a winning Bid advances to an Awarded Contract, all communications regarding this All-Source RFP must be conducted through the IE and will be confidential. Communications may include a meeting or conference call with a Participant, attended by the IE and GPC, to discuss the Participant’s questions regarding the RFP Process or Submission(s), unless the Participant declines such a meeting. The IE is also allowed to conduct conference calls with a Participant, Staff, and GPC to clarify or resolve issues with a Submission or the RFP Process. Staff may, but is not required to, participate in the discussions.
Communication Before Submissions.
 Under the RFP Rule, a Participant may not contact any Evaluation Team member concerning any aspect of this All-Source RFP. Each Participant and interested Person registered on the IE Website may submit questions concerning this All-Source RFP, the RFP Documents, or Submission evaluation on the “Q&A” page of the IE Website. The questions and GPC’s responses will be posted on the IE Website for viewing by all registered users of the IE Website. Participant will have a confidential Bid Book on the IE Website once the Bid Period commences and Participant initiates the Submission process. A Participant may ask Site-specific and Facility-specific questions using the “Messages” feature on the IE Website. Communications submitted through a Bid Book are not seen by other Participants and are only viewed by the Evaluation Team, IE, and Staff. The Evaluation Team will endeavor to promptly respond to each message. Any question posted to the confidential message board that the IE determines to be generic in nature, and not unique to a specific Site or Facility, may be transferred to the public “Q&A” tab on the IE Website.
Communication After Submissions.
Bid Books, Message Board. Once the Bid Period commences and Participant initiates the Submission process, each Participant will have a confidential Bid Book on the IE Website, where Participant posts all RFP deliverables and all messages from IE to Participant are available to Participant. Participant may ask Site-specific and Facility-specific questions using the confidential message board. Questions submitted on the message board are not available to other Participants and are only viewed by the Evaluation Team, the IE, and Staff. The Evaluation Team will reply to each question posted on the message board, after review and consultation with the IE and Staff. All questions determined by the IE to be generic in nature, and not unique to a specific Site or Facility, may be transferred to the “Q&A” page of the IE Website so that all Participants and registered users have the benefit of the question and response.
Listing Determination.
 The status of a Submission is confidential information, and Participants must not disclose the status of any Submission. GPC will not publicly announce the Conforming List, Competitive Tier, Short List, or Release List. The identity of the winning Submission(s) and winning Participant(s) will become public information when GPC requests Certification of the related Awarded Contract or Company-Owned Proposal, if any.
After Execution of the Awarded Contract.
 A winning Participant may not announce its status as a winning Participant or execution of an Awarded Contract via a press release or any other method of public communication without GPC’s prior, express written consent. A winning Participant is responsible for ensuring that its winning Submission status remains confidential and is not announced by any Affiliate, Representative, or contractual party. 
Renewable Resource Awarded Contracts. To the extent an Awarded Contract is for a Facility that includes a Renewable Resource, a Winning Bidder must educate its Affiliates, Representatives, contractual parties, and any other participants in the development of the Facility (e.g., development authorities, county, state, or federal Governmental Authorities) on the potential impact of public statements regarding renewable facilities (e.g., REC claims) and how the public statements may jeopardize the validity of Environmental Attributes that are sold to GPC under the Awarded Contract, which could result in a breach of the Awarded Contract by Seller. Upon execution of the Awarded Contract(s), the Winning Bidder(s) and GPC will work together to determine the timing and content of the official announcement of the winning status of the project and Awarded Contract execution. Upon entering the Awarded Contract, Seller must comply with the provisions of the Awarded Contract concerning any public statements about the Facility, including the RECs, and must ensure its Representatives also comply with these same Awarded Contract provisions. 
Point of Contact.
 Each Submission must include detailed contact information for Participant’s primary point of contact and a secondary point of contact. These persons will serve as the contact between the IE and the Participant when questions and answers are exchanged and will receive authority to access the Participant’s Bid Book on the IE Website. These contact persons must be familiar with all aspects of the Submission process and Submission to efficiently communicate with the IE as necessary and to reduce any delay in communication. Participant must provide notice via the IE Website if there is a change in Participant’s point(s) of contact.
Confidentiality and Photographs for Site Compliance.
Submission Information. Each Bidder must not disclose Bid Information to others, including the ongoing status of its Bid(s) or the information exchanged and discussed between Bidder and GPC, Staff, or the IE (which exchanges and discussions must occur under the guidelines of this All-Source RFP and the RFP Rule), except that Bidder may disclose Bid Information to: (i) Staff; or (ii) Bidder’s Representatives as reasonably necessary for Bidder to submit a Bid in this All-Source RFP, so long as a condition precedent to the permitted disclosure to Bidder’s Representative(s): (a) Bidder must direct its Representative(s) not to disclose Bid Information; and (b) the Representative(s) must be subject to a contractual obligation to maintain confidentiality of Bid Information. If the Representative cannot be made subject to a contractual obligation to maintain confidentiality of Bid Information, Bidder must obtain GPC’s written consent before making the disclosure. 
Bidder’s Confidential Information. GPC will take reasonable precautions and use reasonable efforts to protect any Confidential Information contained in a Bid, so long as Bidder clearly identifies the information as Confidential Information on each page on which it appears. GPC may, however, make Bidder Confidential Information available under applicable state or federal law to Governmental Authorities having jurisdiction over this All-Source RFP. GPC may also release information to: (i) the IE and Staff as needed to monitor this All-Source RFP; (ii) regulated retail Affiliates; (iii) SCS; or (iv) affected entities who have a need to know to assist in Bid evaluation, so long as the entities agree to observe the same care regarding non-disclosure as GPC. Additionally, GPC may, under the terms of the pro forma PPA, share Facility-specific information with the new Facility owner if the Seller assigns or otherwise transfers control of the Facility to a new owner. If the winning Bidder/Seller elects to sell the Facility, GPC may share the winning Bidder’s/Seller’s Confidential Information (e.g., reliability or information on operations) with prospective buyers who are identified by Seller, to ensure future performance in accordance with the PPA. Under no circumstance will GPC (including its Affiliates, and the officers, directors, employees, representatives, or agents of any of them) or the IE or Staff be liable for any damages resulting from any disclosure before, during, or after the RFP Process.
Photographs of Facility or Site. At GPC’s request, Seller must provide GPC with photographs of the Facility or Site that may be used by GPC for verification of Seller’s compliance with this All-Source RFP’s requirements or for informational purposes. Seller grants to GPC and its Representatives, agents, Affiliates, successors, and assigns an irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, and unrestricted right and license to use, duplicate, modify, sublicense, distribute, display, or otherwise engage the photographs and related intellectual property, including the creation of derivative works. Seller represents and warrants that it has the exclusive right to grant the license to GPC for the purposes stated in this All-Source RFP and related documents.
BIDDER ATTRIBUTES
Bidder Information to be Submitted.
 Each Bidder must provide the information described in this Part 6 (Bidder Attributes) at the time of Bid submission. GPC will screen each Bidder on the criteria to ensure basic Bidder qualifications and eligibility.
Financial Metrics. 
 Each Bidder must provide its most recent audited annual report and any 10-Q filings since the period covered in the annual report. If the report and filings are not available, Bidder should note this and provide the latest three years of audited financial statements for itself, Seller Guarantor, and its upstream parent entity (if different than its likely Seller Guarantor). Bidder should also reference the Bid Form for additional information on the financial metrics required. If Bidder can provide any additional details related to its banking relationships or liquidity, GPC will consider those items in the credit evaluation as well. All financial statements, annual reports, and other large documents may be referenced via a website address.
Project Development Experience.
 Each Bidder must provide an executive summary of no more than 5,000 words describing its development experience for the past five years where: (i) Bidder (or, if Bidder is a special purpose entity created for purposes of bidding into this All-Source RFP, Bidder’s parent (either immediate parent or other applicable upstream entity)), was the primary project developer or member of a consortium or joint venture; and (ii) the proposed facility was similar in size, was located in the United States, and utilized the same technology. Such summary must include: (a) the total number of projects and the capability (MW) of each facility Bidder currently owns and operates in the United States; (b) a description of the experience of the principal members of Bidder’s project team; and (c) information on who will be responsible for design, siting, permitting, financing, construction, and, in the case of a PPA Bid, on-going operation and maintenance of the Facility, if known. In the absence of such expertise and experience in any such area, Bidder must demonstrate it has binding arrangements in place with third parties who do possess the requisite expertise and experience and must provide a certification from an independent, registered engineer acceptable to GPC to the effect that the Bidder’s arrangements are sufficiently firm and binding as to provide a comparable level of experience and expertise. At a minimum, GPC will require the successful Bidder(s) who enter into a PPA to demonstrate that they possess, or have binding arrangements with others who possess, current experience greater than three years in operating and maintaining or arranging for the operation and maintenance of similar generation as follows:
For All Bids. Bidders must have experience in the operation and maintenance of the facility technology type they are proposing, or in the alternative, have experience reasonably transferable to the operation and maintenance of the facilities.
Bidder and Contract Counterparty History. 
 Each Bidder must disclose all power purchase agreements, build transfer agreements, or facility purchase agreements to which Bidder or any Affiliate was a party in the past five years that were terminated before the end of the contract term or closing, as applicable, and the reason for early termination. Each Bidder also must list any instances where Bidder or any Affiliate withdrew a project from any solicitation offered by GPC or any of its Affiliates after being identified as part of the Competitive Tier (or equivalent process) in the last five years. Each Bidder must identify and describe any dispute between Bidder or any of its Affiliates and GPC or any of its Affiliates (including all direct and indirect subsidiaries of Southern Company) that: (i) remain unresolved; or (ii) occurred within the last five years but have been resolved. In addition, each Bidder must identify any dispute with other off-takers that have progressed to any claim, litigation, or action that has been initiated with a court, Governmental Authority, or any other formal dispute resolution process. If Bidder or any of its Affiliates currently owe any outstanding past due debt to GPC or one of its Affiliates, Bidder must also disclose this and provide details regarding the reason for non-payment. Before further consideration of such Bidder’s Bid, Bidder may be required to resolve any undisputed outstanding debt to the satisfaction of all parties. 
Union Labor.
 GPC is interested in receiving feedback on Bidder’s use of unionized labor. As part of its Bid, Bidder will be asked to describe its efforts to use unionized labor, and if Bidder has used unionized labor for prior projects during: (i) construction phase; and (ii) during operations of any other facility. If so, Bidder will also be asked to describe any requirements under any project labor agreements imposing requirements to use unionized labor.
Intentional Inclusion. 
 GPC is committed to supporting intentional inclusion within GPC’s own decision-making, hiring and promotion, and daily operations. GPC encourages its counterparties, service providers, consultants, and supply chain vendors to promote similar efforts. To be considered for this non-price factor, Bidder must complete the Intentional Inclusion Certificate found in Exhibit F (Intentional Inclusion Certificate).
SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS
Notice of Intent to Submit APA.
. GPC requests that each Participant intending to offer an APA submits a notice of intent (NOI) using the form available on the IE Website by the date and time recommended in the Solicitation Schedule. Participant must list only one point of contact in the NOI. If Participant intends to submit multiple APA Submissions, Participant may list all potential Submissions on a single NOI. Participant must indicate its proposed technology type for each Submission.
Bid Process.
 Each Submission must be submitted via the Bid Form on the IE Website by no later than the date and time specified in the Solicitation Schedule. If a Bidder discovers an error or omission in the Bid after submitting its Bids but before the Bid Due Date, Bidder must note any change in the electronic filing and the changes must be posted to the Bid Form by no later than 12:00 p.m. ET on the Bid Due Date.
Effect of Bid Submission.
 Each Participant’s Submission will constitute Participant’s acknowledgment and acceptance of all terms, conditions, and requirements of this All-Source RFP, including pro forma contract terms and conditions. GPC is not required to contact any Participant to obtain any omitted information.
Alternative Submissions; Multiple Submissions; Bid Fees.

 Multiple Submissions. Except for Alternative Submissions and Contingent Submissions, GPC will not accept any Submission that is dependent on another Submission’s outcome. 
Alternative Submissions. Each set of Alternative Submissions must maintain the same: (i) Site; (ii) Point of Delivery; (iii) operating characteristics; (iv) performance guarantees, including heat rate, RTE, or other guarantees; and (iv) if applicable, Variable O&M. Each Alternative Submission within a set of Alternative Submissions must be capable of being independently evaluated as a variation of the same proposed Facility. Participant may condition GPC’s selection of an Alternative Submission on the selection of a Contingent Submission.
Contingent Submissions. A Contingent Submission may be used to propose portfolio offers, phased development, shared facilities arrangements, or other Project structures in which the viability of one Facility depends upon the selection of another Facility offered by the same Participant.
Alternative Contingent Submissions. For each Contingent Submission, Participant may submit up to two additional Alternative Contingent Submissions for a total of three Alternative Contingent Submissions. Any Alternative Contingent Submission must relate to the same Site and Point of Delivery as any other Alternative Contingent Submission to which it relates.
Bid Fees; Bid Security. 
Bidder may offer up to three Alternative Submissions under one Bid Fee. Bidder must pay a separate Bid Fee for each Contingent Submission, except that Bidder may pay a single Bid Fee for up to three Alternative Contingent Submissions for the same Facility. Bidder must provide Bid Security for each Contingent Submission. However, for Alternative Contingent Submissions for the same Facility and mutually exclusive Contingent Submissions (i.e., only one of the Contingent Submissions can be accepted), Bidder may post a single Bid Security in an amount equal to the highest Bid Security required among those Contingent Submissions. For clarity, Bidder is not required to post separate Bid Security for each Alternative Contingent Submission relating to the same Facility so long as Bidder posts one Bid Security in the required amount.  
Alternative and Contingent Submission Guidance. Participants must review and comply with the Alternative and Contingent Submission Guidance document available on the IE Website.

Submission Information. 
Submissions must include all applicable information requested on the IE Website and any other information that is necessary for a thorough understanding and evaluation of the Submission. Any Submission that does not contain all the required information on the applicable due date will be subject to rejection by GPC as non-responsive. It is each Participant’s responsibility to submit additional information about its Submission that could further inform GPC’s understanding of the Submission or could materially affect its value. Required Submission information includes the information outlined below.
Facility Name. Due to the need to manage a multitude of projects, and GPC’s experience with counterparties selecting similar or confusing names for projects, GPC may reject a Facility name offered by a Winning Bidder and propose an alternative name. To give Bidder sufficient time to perform due diligence on the Facility name and any proposed special purpose entity name it intends to use as the Awarded Contract counterparty, GPC may request Bidder confirmation of the Facility and counterparty names at the time a Bid advances to the Competitive Tier.
Site Control Affidavit. Each Participant must submit a notarized Site Control Affidavit that affirms Participant has obtained Site Control during the PPA Term or Facility Design Life, as applicable. The form Site Control Affidavit is attached as Exhibit C (Form of Site Control Affidavit and Landowner Confirmation). Participant may be required to submit further evidence of Site Control, as and when deemed necessary by GPC.
Bidder Variable Interest Entity Certification. Depending on the PPA Term and the business structure, a PPA Bidder may choose to adopt accounting and tax rules that may require: (i) that a PPA, or components of the PPA, be accounted for by GPC as a lease; or (ii) Seller under the PPA be consolidated as a VIE onto GPC’s books. Because GPC is unwilling to be subject to accounting or tax treatment that results from VIE treatment, each Bidder is required to certify, using the form found in Exhibit I (VIE Certification), its independent belief that the Bidder’s Bid will most likely not require the Seller at any time over the proposed PPA Term to deconsolidate on its books and records any assets, liabilities, cash flow, profits, or losses where GPC is determined to be the Primary Beneficiary.
Financial and Business Data. Each PPA Bidder with a Bid advanced to the Short List must also agree to make available all financial and business data associated with Seller, the Facility, and the PPA that GPC would need to make its independent accounting determinations. Such information may include, but may not be limited to, data supporting the economic life, the fair value, investment tax credits associated with, or other costs associated with the Facility, including debt specific to the asset proposed. Financial data contained in Bidder’s financial statements (e.g., income statements or balance sheets) may also be required.  
Organizational Chart. Each Bid must include an organizational chart that identifies (by name and state of organization) all related Affiliates or special purpose entities. If Bidder intends to form a new special purpose entity or subsidiary to become the Awarded Contract counterparty, GPC requests that Bidder disclose this intent as part of the Bid, and in any case, it must be disclosed by no later than the Day after Bidder is notified of the Bid’s advancement to the Short List. Any Bidder using or planning to use a special purpose entity or subsidiary as the Awarded Contract counterparty (i.e., Seller), must include a proposed organizational chart clearly showing the relationship to the special purpose entity or subsidiary, as applicable. 
Registration in Georgia. Except for APA Sellers offering a Facility outside of the state of Georgia, Seller under the Awarded Contract must register and be in active and compliant standing with the Office of the Georgia Secretary of State, authorizing Seller to do business in Georgia before the time of Awarded Contract execution.
Pro Forma APA or PPA Markup Required.
 In accordance with the RFP Rule, prospective Bidders in this All-Source RFP were given an opportunity to comment on the RFP and pro forma contracts during a public review and comment period. Upon Commission approval of the RFP Documents, the concepts and material risk allocation provisions of the pro forma APA and PPAs are non-negotiable except as provided in this Section 7.5.7 (Pro Forma APA or PPA Markup Required). Each Bid must include a mark-up of the pro forma contract that most closely applies to the Bid with: (i) all blank spaces (including exhibits) completely filled in except those that are to be completed by GPC; (ii) any proposed change to the pro forma APA or PPA (whichever applicable) shown with specificity in the mark-up and accompanied by a summary of changes; and (iii) a statement by Bidder that the terms and conditions of the applicable pro forma APA or PPA, as non-materially modified by the Bidder, are acceptable to Bidder. If the Bid is conditioned on any change to the applicable pro forma APA or PPA, then Bidder must expressly so state and must provide the specific language proposed by Bidder by redlining a copy of the appropriate pro forma APA or PPA attached to the Bid, such that it shows the specific additions (bold and underlined) and deletions (strike-through) that Bidder proposes. 
Pro Forma PPAs. GPC developed four pro forma PPAs, with generally consistent provisions; however, Bidder must note that this All-Source RFP reflects general terms and conditions and each pro forma PPA reflects technology-specific terms and conditions applicable to its generation type. For any deviation between the terms and conditions of this RFP and the terms and conditions of the applicable pro forma PPA, the terms and conditions of the specific pro forma PPA will control.
Assumptions. The four pro forma PPAs include: (i) CC New Resource; (ii) CT New Resource; (iii) ESS with Renewable Resource; and (iv) Standalone ESS, including an option to pair the ESS with a Renewable Resource committed under a separate PPA. For clarity, a Bidder offering to pair a new ESS with a Renewable Resource committed under a separate PPA with GPC must use the pro forma PPA applicable to Standalone ESS, which includes optionality to pair the ESS with an existing Renewable Resource. The four pro forma PPAs are based on several assumptions that may or may not apply to a Bid. Examples of assumptions are: (a) the proposed Facility is a New Resource; (b) the Seller is not itself a Creditworthy entity; (c) the Bid offers 100% of a Facility’s output capability; (d) the CC pro forma PPA assumes a base operating mode and two supplemental modes designated as Tier 1 and Tier 2; and (e) the ESS pro forma PPAs assume the ESS is a BESS. Deviation from one or more of these assumptions may require modification of the applicable pro forma PPA. For more details on these assumptions, please see the applicable pro forma PPA.
Conversion of CT or CT PPA for Existing Resource. If Bidder offers a Bid to deliver capacity and energy from a CC or CT Existing Resource, including any Partial Output Bid, Bidder must mark up the PPA, per Section 7.5.7 (Pro Forma APA or PPA Markup Required), to convert the applicable CC or CT pro forma PPA, which has a New Resource assumption, to a PPA for an Existing Resource. Instructions on how to make this conversion are found in the “Existing Resource Modifications to CC/CT Pro Forma PPAs” document located on the IE Website. GPC will review and consider Facility-specific changes that are necessary to conform the pro forma PPA to the characteristics of the Facility and GPC’s offtake rights, but GPC will not accept any deviation from the pro forma PPAs that alter the material risk allocation or impair GPC’s first priority right to the Contracted Capacity.
Material Conformance. Each Bid must conform to the applicable pro forma APA or PPA in all material respects, except where: (i) Bidder offers revisions that GPC, in coordination with Staff and the IE, determines do not materially affect the value to customers; or (ii) the pro forma contract assumptions do not conform to the specific characteristics of a Bid. For example, the pro forma ESS with Renewable Resource PPA assumes the Renewable Resource that is paired with the ESS is a solar facility. A Bidder offering a CAES Facility, or an ESS with Renewable Resource technology other than solar, must mark up the pro forma PPA to reflect its proposed Facility parameters. Another example would be if a Bidder’s Bid conforms to RFP requirements and the Bid offers a fuel other than natural gas, such as biomass, then Bidder must propose changes to the applicable natural gas-fired pro forma PPA to the extent needed to conform the pro forma PPA’s provisions to the proposed fuel.
Additional APA Information.
 A Bidder submitting an APA Bid must be prepared to provide all necessary information by Bid Due Date to support commencement of the initial due diligence assessment. Exhibit A (Due Diligence Phases and Fees Overview (APA Bids Only)) outlines the due diligence review process, which proceeds in three stages and divides the required APA due diligence fees accordingly. An APA Bidder may be asked to provide additional data at any time during any of the due diligence review periods. Data must be reasonably available to be copied and reviewed by GPC, and the APA Bidder must work with GPC to ensure timely sharing of information (i.e., five Business Days unless otherwise agreed).
APA Conformance. After an APA Bid advances to the Short List, GPC and the Bidder will meet to further conform Project-specific provisions of the APA. The IE and Staff have the right, but not the obligation, to attend all meetings for the purpose of monitoring.
Bid Validity.
 Each Bid must remain valid until the earlier of: (i) the date this RFP concludes; (ii) the date GPC files the applicable executed Awarded Contract with the Commission; or (iii) Bid withdrawal or release.
No Changes after Bid Period Concludes.
 Once the Bid Period closes, Participant will not be allowed to make any change to the Submission that would impact GPC’s evaluation of the Submission, except as described in Section 4.4 (Refreshed Submission Process), Section 7.8.1 (Submission Deficiencies), and Section 7.8.2 (Bid or Company-Owned Proposal Errors). 
Submission Deficiencies.
 After the Submission deadline, the IE will review key elements of each Bid and any Company-Owned Proposal to screen for errors and omissions and, if necessary, confirm those elements with the Participant. Any Submission that does not satisfy the applicable requirements of this All-Source RFP will be considered a Deficient Submission and may be released. In consultation with Staff and the Evaluation Team, the IE will provide Participant an opportunity to cure deficiencies. After that occurs, a Bid or Company-Owned Proposal that is not cured will be identified as a Deficient Submission and rejected. After the Bid Due Date, no Participant may change its pricing or revise its Bid or Company-Owned Proposal on its own initiative. After consulting with Staff and the IE, the Evaluation Team may request that a Bid or Company-Owned Proposal be revised to obtain the best value for GPC’s customers. Any requested revision of a Bid or Company-Owned Proposal will be reviewed by Staff and the IE before being addressed with the respective Participant.
Bid or Company-Owned Proposal Errors.
 GPC will not permit any modification of Bids or Company-Owned Proposals after the cure period unless correction of the error or omission is in the best interest of GPC’s customers and will not harm the RFP Process, as determined by GPC in consultation with the IE and Staff. All modification requests must be made through the IE Website.
Bid Certification.
 If Bidder is a business entity, an authorized officer of Bidder’s company must electronically sign the submitted Bid(s) through the Bid Form.
Duty to Notify GPC of Issues Impacting Submissions.
 After Participant submits the Submission, Participant must promptly notify GPC in writing through the IE Website of any issue, event, or other development that impacts, or would reasonably be expected to impact, the development, construction, or completion of the Facility associated with the Submission.
Bid Assignments.
 Any Bid Assignment must comply in all respects with the provisions of Exhibit E (Bid Assignment Guidelines). Any purported Bid Assignment that does not comply in all respects with the provisions of Exhibit E will be void.
Bid Withdrawal.
 Bidder may withdraw its Bid by submitting a Bid withdrawal notice via the “Messages” feature on the IE Website. If Bidder withdraws its Bid after the Bid submission deadline, Bidder will not be permitted to reopen the Bid at a later date. Bidder will not be entitled to a refund of any fees or any Bid Security if Bidder withdraws its Bid. 
BID EVALUATION AND AWARDED CONTRACTS; COMPANY-OWNED PROPOSAL EVALUATION 
Staff and IE Oversight/Evaluation.
 In accordance with the RFP Rule, Staff and the IE actively and contemporaneously monitor all aspects of GPC’s evaluation process for transparency purposes. Staff and the IE will review all Submissions and conduct an independent evaluation of the Capacity Resources offered to GPC in this All-Source RFP. Staff and the IE are permitted access to all documents and information utilized by GPC in its evaluation. GPC, Staff, and IE will meet to discuss and finalize the Competitive Tier and, after further evaluation of the Competitive Tier, the Short List, including Bids identified for Awarded Contract award and any Company-Owned Proposal identified for inclusion on the Short List.
Criteria. 
All Submissions in this All-Source RFP will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation criteria and structure described in Exhibit G (Overview of Evaluation Methodology). GPC reserves the right to contact any Participant through the IE Website to request additional information on any aspect of a Submission. GPC also reserves the right to request that the IE contact any Participant for additional information or to cure a deficiency identified in a Submission.
Initial Review.
 Submissions that are complete and conform to RFP requirements will be ranked and screened on price to eliminate Submissions that are clearly not competitive before detailed economic modeling is performed. 
Competitive Tier Identified.
 Under the oversight of the IE and Staff, GPC will evaluate all Submissions and determine a Competitive Tier that consists of the most competitive Submissions. An appropriate selection of Submissions meeting GPC’s requirements will advance as the Competitive Tier for additional evaluation. A Participant whose Submission(s) advanced to the Competitive Tier or Short List, or is released from this RFP, will be notified in accordance with the Solicitation Schedule. In addition, all Submissions in the Competitive Tier will undergo a comprehensive environmental review to ensure compliance with the requirements of this RFP, including the Environmental Assurances Guidance Document.
Bid Lists.
 In accordance with the Solicitation Schedule, upon completion of the Competitive Tier evaluation, Participant will be notified if its Submission is on the Short List, Reserve List, or Release List. Using the IE Website, the Evaluation Team will contact each Bidder with a Bid advanced to the Short List to finalize and execute the PPA or APA, as applicable. A Submission on the Reserve List is a Submission that is essentially on a waiting list that will continue to be under evaluation and may move on to the Short List if a Short List Participant withdraws or is unable to proceed. A Submission on the Release List was determined to be non-competitive and will no longer be considered for advancement in this All-Source RFP. Release List determinations are final and will not be reconsidered. By the end of the RFP Process, all Submissions not placed on the Release List and not advanced for contracting will be placed on the Reserve List. When GPC executes the winning PPAs or APAs and files the executed Awarded Contracts with the Commission, all unadvanced Bids and Company-Owned Proposals will be placed on the Release List.
Short List. After full evaluation of the Competitive Tier Submissions, successful Competitive Tier Submissions will advance to the Short List. Short-listed Submissions will be re-evaluated and compared before GPC finalizes any decision regarding its choice of resource(s) to meet identified needs. Each Bidder with a Bid advanced to the Short List for further evaluation must also provide the following information, as applicable and if requested by GPC in consultation with Staff and IE: (i) updates to the construction schedule; (ii) a current Site plan; (iii) equipment delivery schedules; (iv) draft certificates of insurance; and (v) any financial and business data associated with the Seller, the Facility, or the PPA or APA, as applicable, that GPC would need to independently make necessary accounting determinations. Requested information may include data supporting the economic life, the fair value, investment tax credits associated with the Facility, or other costs associated with the Facility, including debt specific to the asset proposed. Financial data contained in Bidder’s financial statements (e.g., income statements or balance sheets) may also be required.
Awarded Contract Execution.
 GPC will award and execute Awarded Contracts with the Winning Bidders whose Bids are on the Short List. Upon finalization of the Short List, Winning Bidders will be notified and asked to meet with GPC and the IE, and with Staff who choose to participate, to discuss execution of the Awarded Contract. A Winning Bidder will enter into the applicable and conforming pro forma PPA or conforming APA with GPC. GPC and Winning Bidder will coordinate to execute the PPA or APA, as applicable, by the date set forth in the Solicitation Schedule. 
Rejection of Submissions.
 GPC reserves the right, without qualification and in its sole discretion, to reject as non-responsive any Submission for failure to meet any RFP requirement. If GPC discovers that any Bidder violated this All-Source RFP or otherwise violated the spirit and intent of this All-Source RFP, GPC has the right to reject any related Bids, which may also further affect the Bidder’s participation in any future programs offered by GPC. By way of example and not by limitation, the following will constitute a non-responsive Bid: (i) a Bid offering non-firm capacity; (ii) an uncured, incomplete, or non-specific Bid; or (iii) a Bid that fails to materially comply with the provisions of the applicable pro forma PPA. GPC further reserves the right, without qualification and in its sole discretion, to decline to enter a PPA or APA with any Bidder for any reason. GPC will not refund any Bid Fee or other costs associated with any Bid for any reason, including GPC’s rejection of the Bid or failure by Bidder to execute an Awarded Contract. 
Rejection of Bid for Failure to Respond or Comply with Deadlines. GPC reserves the right to reject any Deficient Bid at any time if Bidder fails to submit required information, make a required payment, or otherwise provide to GPC any required deliverable by the deadline set forth in this All-Source RFP (and any date in the Solicitation Schedule as revised, if applicable). A question asked by a Bidder regarding a deadline does not extend the deadline. If a Bid is found to be a Deficient Bid, then it may be placed on the Release List and released from this All-Source RFP. GPC is not required to contact any Bidder to obtain any omitted information.
Rejection of Bid for Environmental Concerns. GPC reserves the right to reject any Bid at any time if the siting or construction of the proposed Facility presents an environmental or archeological impact or risk that: (i) cannot be mitigated or overcome within the timeframe of this All-Source RFP; or (ii) potentially undermines GPC’s environmental stewardship efforts. The archeological risks and impacts may include, for example, the presence or discovery of any archaeological, historical, religious, or cultural site, place, artifact, or monument.
Rejection of Bid for Failure to Demonstrate Site Control. GPC reserves the right to reject any Bid if Bidder fails to demonstrate Site Control at the time of Bid submission or at any other time during the RFP Process. 
Rejection of a Bidder’s Request that Conflicts with GPC Policy. If Bidder requests that GPC take any action that conflicts with GPC’s business policies and procedures, GPC will not honor Bidder’s request and will inform Bidder of the conflict. In such case, GPC may reject the Bid.
GPC Discretion in Contracting.
 GPC reserves the right, without qualification and in consultation with the IE and Staff, to reject any, all, or portions of Bids received for failure to meet any criteria, and further reserves the right, without qualification and at its sole discretion, and in consultation with the IE and Staff, to decline to enter into an Awarded Contract with any Bidder. Any Bidder who submits a Bid in response to this All-Source RFP waives the right to claim any recourse against GPC or any of its Affiliates or IE for either rejection of Bidder’s Bid(s) or for failure to execute an Awarded Contract for any reason.
Fees Nonrefundable.
 Bid Fees submitted by any Bidder will not be refunded (unless otherwise determined in the sole discretion of GPC) in the case of any modification or withdrawal of this All-Source RFP, rejection of any Bid, or failure to execute an Awarded Contract.
QUALIFYING FACILITIES
Qualifying Facility Participation.
 In accordance with PURPA and applicable Commission Orders in Dockets 4822 and 19279, Qualifying Facilities (QFs) may be eligible for a capacity payment because GPC seeks to fill a capacity need through this All-Source RFP. QFs sized larger than 30 MW must compete in this All-Source RFP, including submission of a Bid by the Bid Due Date. QFs sized 30 MW or less must submit a QF notice of intent (available on the IE Website) in accordance with the Solicitation Schedule. Eligibility for capacity payments is subject to execution of a Standard Offer Power Purchase Agreement and compliance with applicable availability requirements. Additional details regarding QF participation requirements are available on the IE Website and GPC’s QF Program website (https://www.georgiapower.com/business/products-programs/business-solutions/qualifying-facilities.html).

CERTIFICATION
Awarded Contract Certification.
 Following completion of the All-Source RFP evaluation and award process, GPC will seek Commission Certification, under O.C.G.A. § 46-3A-4, of each Awarded Contract executed with this All-Source RFP. The Certification process may take place under a separate Commission Docket and may take up to six Months to complete, unless otherwise expedited by the Commission Procedural and Scheduling Order. The Parties’ continued performance of an Awarded Contract is conditioned on the Commission issuing a certificate approving the Awarded Contract in a timely manner without material qualification or condition adversely affecting GPC or Seller; provided, however, that this condition subsequent does not excuse, limit, or otherwise affect Seller’s liability for any breach occurring before Commission Certification. If the Commission does not issue a certificate approving the Awarded Contract in accordance with the previous sentence, the Awarded Contract will provide that GPC or Seller may terminate the PPA without any further obligation. In addition to GPC’s Awarded Contract obligations being contingent on Commission approval, GPC’s obligations are also contingent upon GPC continuing to have a need for capacity and energy for the identified need years, as confirmed by the Commission.
FERC Acceptance. Performance of an Awarded Contract is also conditioned upon, if required by applicable law, FERC issuing an order accepting the Awarded Contract in a timely manner and without material qualification or condition adversely affecting either party to the Awarded Contract; otherwise, the Awarded Contract will provide that either party may terminate the Awarded Contract without any further legal obligation.   
Company-Owned Proposal Certification.
 In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 46-3A-5, and under Commission Rule 515-3-4-.07(2), if a Company-Owned Proposal advances, it will be submitted for Certification together with other winning Bids, and the IE will testify regarding its evaluation of the Company-Owned Proposal. The Commission’s certificate approving any Company-Owned Proposal will set forth the not-to-exceed cost, which, like the certified cost of any PPA or asset purchase agreement under which GPC acquires a Facility, may not otherwise change, except as allowed by law under O.C.G.A. § 46-3A-7, and only with the Commission’s express approval.


Exhibit A – Due Diligence Phases and Fees Overview (APA Bids Only)
Bid Information. 
Identification of Critical Due Diligence Topics for First Due Diligence Phase. At the time of Bid submission, an APA Bidder must provide the APA items with accompanying documents as detailed in the Due Diligence Checklist available on the IE Website. This Exhibit A (Due Diligence Phases and Fees Overview (APA Bids Only)) describes critical due diligence information that Bidders must submit by the Bid Due Date for the Evaluation Team to review in the first due diligence phase (“Phase One Due Diligence”). Bidder must also identify known plant equipment and operational concerns (e.g., vibrations, recurring problems or failures, needed maintenance, cracked turbine blades) and known legal or environmental issues concerning the Facility so key issues that could affect life-cycle cost or Facility reliability can be addressed early in the due diligence process.
Initial Economic Screen ($20,000 Fee).
Bid Fee. Each Bidder must submit a non-refundable Bid Fee ($20,000) with each Bid in accordance with RFP Section 7.4.5 (Bid Fees) before the Evaluation Team will begin evaluating the Bid. 
Screening Overview. If a Bid advances past the initial review described in RFP Section 8.3 (Initial Review), the Bid will proceed through the additional due diligence steps outlined in the following sections of this Exhibit A.
Phase One Due Diligence ($50,000 Fee).
Fee Requirement. Bidder must submit a Phase One Due Diligence Fee of fifty thousand dollars ($50,000) in addition to the required Bid Fee ($20,000) by no later than the Bid Due Date shown in the Solicitation Schedule. The total initial payment required for APA Bids is seventy thousand dollars ($70,000), which is the sum of: (i) the  Bid Fee ($20,000); plus (ii) the Phase One Due Diligence Fee ($50,000). 
Phase One Due Diligence Overview. As soon as the initial review described in RFP Section 8.3 (Initial Review) is complete, the Evaluation Team will begin its Phase One Due Diligence review. Phase One Due Diligence will consist of “fatal flaw assessment” to determine if there are significant issues with the APA Bid that would call into question the value of the asset. The Phase One Due Diligence review will be preliminary and will include the following: 
Technical and engineering review of Due Diligence Checklist and accompanying documents, including review of major equipment and balance of plant components. 
For items requested in the Due Diligence Checklist and required accompanying documents that Bidder did not provide with the Bid Submission, Bidder must explain in writing why Bidder failed to submit the information. The Solicitation Schedule was condensed compared to prior capacity RFPs. As a result, the timeframe for Phase One Due Diligence will be shorter. Therefore, it is critical that Bidder provides the Evaluation Team the information requested in the Due Diligence Checklist by the Bid Due Date. 
Review of independent engineering report. 
Site design and initial engineering technical review. 
Refund or Credit of Unused Fee. If GPC does not expend the entire Phase One Due Diligence Fee, GPC will refund the unused portion to Bidder or credit the balance as payment toward the Phase Two Due Diligence Fee, as applicable.
Phase two due diligence (Up to $800,000 Fee).
Fee Requirements. If the Bid satisfies the Phase One Due Diligence review and advances to Conforming List, then, to proceed with the second due diligence phase (“Phase Two Due Diligence”), Bidder must submit an initial Phase Two Due Diligence Fee of four hundred thousand dollars ($400,000), less any credit from the Phase One Due Diligence Fee that is applied toward the initial Phase Two Due Diligence Fee. To proceed to Phase Two Due Diligence, Bidder must pay the initial Phase Two Due Diligence Fee by the deadline stated in the Solicitation Schedule. If the costs of Phase Two Due Diligence exceed the initial Phase Two Due Diligence Fee amount of four hundred thousand dollars ($400,000), the Evaluation Team will request from Bidder a second Phase Two Due Diligence Fee of up to four hundred thousand dollars ($400,000). GPC will notify Bidder of the required Phase Two Due Diligence Fee amount, and Bidder must submit the requested portion of the Phase Two Due Diligence Fee by no later than five Business Days after receipt of any GPC request for payment of all or any portion of the second Phase Two Due Diligence Fee. The total Phase Two Due Diligence Fee will not exceed $800,000, which is the sum of: (i) the initial Phase Two Due Diligence Fee ($400,000); plus (ii) the second Phase Two Due Diligence Fee ($400,000). 
Phase Two Due Diligence Overview. In addition to a detailed review of all pertinent documentation associated with any APA Bid, Phase Two Due Diligence will require on-Site visits by IE, Staff, and GPC, including GPC representatives with experience in areas required for an adequate assessment of the proposed resource, including the following:
Generation Procurement
Technical Services
Operations & Maintenance
Environmental and Natural Resources
During Phase Two Due Diligence, the Evaluation Team will continue its review of additional documentation provided by Bidder, including: 
Bidder’s proposed APA mark-ups;
Site-specific documentation (e.g., permits, surveys, EPC information); and
All available existing and proposed legal documents impacting the transaction (initial review).
Refund or Credit of Unused Fee. If GPC does not expend the entire second Phase Two Due Diligence Fee, GPC will refund the unused portion to Bidder or apply the balance as a credit toward the Phase Three Due Diligence Fee, as applicable.
Phase three due diligence ($135,000 Fee).
Fee Requirement. If the Bid satisfies the Phase Two Due Diligence review, and if Bid advances to the Short List, Bidder must submit the Phase Three Due Diligence Fee of one hundred thirty-five thousand dollars ($135,000), less any credit from the Phase Two Due Diligence Fee, to proceed to the third due diligence phase (“Phase Three Due Diligence”) and remain on the Short List. The Phase Three Due Diligence Fee is due no later than five Business Days after Short List notification. 
In addition to a review of all pertinent documentation associated with any Bid, the need and extent of Phase Three Due Diligence review will depend upon the results of earlier due diligence phases and the extent of any area requiring further assessment. Phase Three Due Diligence will be detailed and include the following:
Detailed risk assessment.
Accounting, finance, and tax review (including any expected tax credits or impacts).
Federal regulatory strategy and assessment.
Final, detailed legal review of all existing and proposed legal documents impacting or regarding the transaction.
Possible on-Site visits by the IE, Staff and GPC team, including personnel from all GPC areas required for an adequate assessment of the proposed resource. 
Refund or Credit of Unused Fee. If GPC does not expend the entire Phase Three Due Diligence Fee, GPC will refund the unused portion to Bidder or apply the balance as a credit toward the Winner’s Fee, as applicable.
Fee Cap; Bid Bond.
Winning Bids; Bid Security Return. If Bidder and GPC execute an Awarded Contract, Bidder must pay all Due Diligence Fees, up to a maximum of $985,000. GPC will not release Bid Security until Due Diligence Fees are settled. 
Bid Security Forfeiture for Bidder Withdraw. If Bidder withdraws its Bid, GPC will return any unused portion of the Due Diligence Fees paid, if any remaining, and Bidder will forfeit the Bid Security in accordance with RFP Section 4.8 (Bid Security). 
Due Diligence Fees Wiring Instructions
Wiring Instructions. Bidder must pay to GPC all Due Diligence Fees described in this Exhibit A in accordance with the wiring instructions available on the IE Website. Due Diligence fees sent to any other address will be rejected.

Exhibit B – Interconnection and Delivery Requirements
Each Participant is responsible for determining all transmission interconnection and delivery-related rules, practices, and policies with which Participant must comply. Each Submission must comply with the general requirements outlined in Part 1 (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements – General) of this Exhibit B (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements) and with one of the interconnection options described in either Part 2 (Interconnection with the Southern Company Transmission System (>40 kV)), Part 3 (Interconnection of a Non-ESS Facility to the Electric System of an ITS Participant (>40 kV)), or Part 4 (Interconnection of a Non-ESS Facility Outside the STT (PPA Bidders Only)) of this Exhibit B. 
Interconnection and Delivery Requirements – General
The following interconnection requirements apply to all Submissions, regardless of Facility location.
Transmission Projected Commercial Operation Date. GPC may decline to advance a Submission to the Short List or to execute an Awarded Contract with any Bidder if, in GPC’s opinion, the transmission facilities cannot be constructed in time to achieve Commercial Operation or Closing, as applicable, by the date set forth in the Solicitation Schedule. Except for the provision in Section 2.8 (Facility Interconnecting Directly to GPC) for a Facility interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission System via GPC, Participant assumes all interconnection and delivery lead-time risk (if applicable) to meet the RCOD or RCD, as applicable.
Submission Price Assumptions. If the Facility’s POI is not on the Southern Company Transmission System, each Submission must state the assumptions regarding interconnection and delivery costs that are included in the Submission price. Specifically, each Submission must include details of these costs and refer to any completed or active Interconnection Study results related to the Facility.
Submission Lead-Time Assumptions. Each Submission must describe the proposed Facility’s current status within the applicable interconnection process and Participant’s ability to meet the RCOD, or RCD in the case of an APA, based upon the applicable interconnection process timeline.
Interconnection Agreement Required. Each winning Participant must enter into an IA with the appropriate Interconnection Provider, depending on the geographic location and interconnection configuration of the Facility. Each Participant must contact the appropriate Interconnection Provider to obtain all relevant information and interconnection requirements. A Submission in response to this All-Source RFP does not constitute an interconnection request or an IA. Participant is solely responsible for all fees, deposits, and other charges regarding Participant’s interconnection request and the IA. Any Facility other than one that is outside the SBAA is prohibited from delivering output to the Point of Delivery that exceeds the lesser of the generating/discharge capacity or the Interconnection Limit.
Timing and Notification of Initiating Interconnection Process (New Facility). At the time of Submission, Participant must indicate if there is an existing interconnection request for the Facility (either in active study stage or if there is an IA that is in suspension), and if so, Participant also must identify the Interconnection Provider, request number/identifier, and status. For Facilities not interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission System, Participants are responsible for understanding the interconnection requirements of the applicable Interconnection Provider and initiating the application and study process to comply with the RCOD or RCD requirements of this RFP. For Facilities interconnecting to the Georgia ITS, see also Part 3 (Interconnection of a Non-ESS Facility to the Electric System of an ITS Participant (>40 kV)); for Facilities interconnecting to neither the Southern Company Transmission System nor the Georgia ITS, see also Part 4 (Interconnection of a Non-ESS Facility Outside Both the Southern Company Transmission System and Georgia ITS (PPA Bidders Only)). Regardless of the Interconnection Provider, if Participant has an IA in suspension, by no later than seven Days after notification that the Submission has advanced to the Short List, Participant must initiate the process with the appropriate Interconnection Provider to move out of suspension and back to active status. Further, Participant is responsible for understanding applicable timing requirements associated with submitting an interconnection request and obtaining an Interconnection Agreement from the applicable Interconnection Provider and any related risk to meeting the RCOD, or RCD in the case of an APA, under this RFP.  
Interconnection with the Southern Company Transmission System (>40 kV)
The following requirements apply to a Submission for a Facility interconnecting to the transmission system of GPC or one of its regulated electric utility Affiliates (i.e., Alabama Power or Mississippi Power) with a Point of Interconnection at greater than 40 kV.
Procedure Guidance. If the Facility will interconnect to the Southern Company Transmission System, Participant’s interconnection request will be subject to the rules set forth in FERC Order No. 2023 (“Order 2023”), as described below: 
Annual Cluster Study. Absent further guidance regarding Order 2023, all Participants with Submissions advanced to the Competitive Tier must submit a complete and valid interconnection request by no later than the date necessary for inclusion in the 2026 Annual Cluster Study, except for Participants offering Facilities that (i) will request and are eligible for a Surplus Interconnection Service, (ii) have a valid IA, or (iii) completed the 2025 Annual Cluster Study.
Surplus Interconnection Service. Participant may be eligible to interconnect its proposed Facility using Surplus Interconnection Service under the OATT and pursuant to a surplus interconnection service agreement (“SISA”). “Surplus Interconnection Service” allows a facility to utilize unused interconnection capacity at an existing POI, without requiring new Network Upgrades, provided certain criteria are met. Participant’s eligibility depends on the availability of unused transmission rights under an existing LGIA and whether the proposed Facility meets the technical and operational requirements set forth in applicable FERC regulations and OATT. In general, the Surplus Interconnection Service process is as follows:
Participant must identify an existing LGIA with available unused interconnection capacity that may accommodate the proposed project.
Participant must submit a Surplus Interconnection Service request through Southern Companies’ OASIS, in accordance with Attachment V of the OATT and applicable FERC Order 845 and Order 2023 provisions, and provide all required information.
SCS will conduct a Surplus Interconnection System Impact Study to determine if the Facility can be accommodated using the existing interconnection service without Network Upgrades. If upgrades are needed, the Facility is not eligible for Surplus Interconnection Service.
If the Facility is eligible for Surplus Interconnection Service, Participant must execute a SISA. If Participant is not the interconnection service customer under the LGIA through which Surplus Interconnection Service is offered: (a) the existing interconnection service customer must also execute the SISA; and (b) Participant must demonstrate its right to use interconnection facilities through a shared facilities agreement. 
Participant is solely responsible for: (i) evaluating Participant’s eligibility for Surplus Interconnection Service; and (ii) initiating and completing the Surplus Interconnection Service request process in a timely manner consistent with the Solicitation Schedule. 
Evaluation Assumptions. Submission evaluation will assume that large generator interconnection procedures (“LGIP”) apply and that Participant has executed or will execute a large generator interconnection agreement (“LGIA”). The Southern Company Transmission System includes facilities owned by GPC or one of its regulated electric utility Affiliates (Alabama Power or Mississippi Power). The prompt submission of an accurate and complete application and prompt return of agreements will reduce the overall timeframe of the interconnection process. Each Participant must determine all rules, practices, policies, and timelines with which its Facility must comply to interconnect with the Southern Company Transmission System. Participant may obtain additional information on Southern Company’s OASIS website at: http://www.oatioasis.com/SOCO/index.html.
Participant Cost Responsibility. If the Facility will interconnect with the Southern Company Transmission System, Participant is responsible for all Interconnection Study-related costs, in addition to the interconnection costs and risk up to the POI. Interconnection costs generally include equipment such as the Facility generator step-up (“GSU”) transformer (for conversion up to the interconnecting voltage level), Facility-side generator interrupting device, all Station Service equipment, tie-line (which carries electrical power and communications), any additional equipment (such as a utility-owned interrupting device and metering needed to connect to the transmission facilities), Network Upgrades beyond the POI that are directly assigned (e.g. system protection ), as well as any additional real property for the interconnection substation and access and any operation and maintenance expenses and administrative costs. In addition, if applicable, Participant is responsible for the cost, risk, and coordination of all Affected System Upgrades. It is Participant’s responsibility to determine and consider all information regarding interconnection costs in preparing its Submission.
Interconnection Impacts. 
Southern Company Transmission System Interconnection Costs. Interconnection impacts to the Electric System are unique to the specific design and location of each Facility and may require new or modified equipment beyond the POI. For a Facility interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission System, any interconnection cost for new or modified equipment on the Southern Company Transmission System beyond the POI (e.g., refundable “Network Upgrades” under the LGIP/LGIA) will be imputed to the Submission during the evaluation and should not be included in the Submission price. However, as stated in Section 2.3 (Participant Cost Responsibility) any cost associated with Affected System Upgrades are solely Participant’s responsibility and will not be reimbursed by GPC. 
SCS LGIA Costs. A winning Participant (e.g., Seller) may be required under the terms of its SCS LGIA to fund or provide security for new or modified equipment beyond the POI (interconnection costs beyond the POI that are refundable “Network Upgrades” per the LGIP/LGIA). However, if Seller incurs the interconnection-related costs for new or modified equipment on the Southern Company Transmission System beyond the POI, after the Facility achieves Commercial Operation or Closing is achieved, as applicable, the costs will be refunded to Seller or security will be released in accordance with LGIA terms and Southern OATT.
Affected System Interconnection Costs. If a winning Submission has interconnection impacts to any Affected System, such that the Affected System must add, modify, or upgrade its Electric System, Participant must coordinate with the Affected System with respect to identifying, planning, and construction of, and payment of costs for, the additions, modifications, or upgrades. Participants must contemplate the schedule and cost impacts in each Submission. Any interconnection costs related to the Affected System are Participant’s sole responsibility and will not be reimbursed by GPC. Any reimbursement for these costs is a matter strictly between the Affected System and Participant.
Delivery Impacts. For Submissions advanced to the Competitive Tier, GPC will develop a cost estimate for Electric System improvements, if any, to the Southern Company Transmission System, the Georgia ITS, or both, that are necessary to deliver the energy from the POI to GPC’s customers. These costs will be imputed to the Submission. 
Short-Term Network Service. Depending on the particular location of the proposed Facility, GPC may be able to obtain Short-Term Network Service earlier than it can obtain long-term firm network service for delivery of the Facility’s output to GPC’s customers. If studies indicate that Short-Term Network Service could be available that would allow a Submission to advance to the Short List, GPC will inform Participant as part of the evaluation process after Competitive Tier announcement.
Construction of Southern Company Transmission System Facilities. Any Electric System improvement, modification, or new facility that will become part of the Southern Company Transmission System must be owned by, and will be designed, procured, and constructed by, as applicable, GPC, Alabama Power, or Mississippi Power.
Facility Interconnecting Directly to GPC. The following provisions apply only to a Facility that is not yet interconnected to GPC at the time of Participant’s Submission.
Land and Property Rights. A winning Participant whose Facility will interconnect with GPC must timely coordinate with GPC’s land acquisition department to obtain and provide to GPC, at Participant’s cost, suitable real property (fee simple or easement, as will be designated during the Interconnection Study process) in an acceptable location for the Interconnection Facilities, along with an Access Route to the ICF Site acceptable to GPC, as well as any necessary encroachment agreement, consent, or similar document. All necessary property right documents must be acceptable to GPC and on its standard terms and conditions, and all property rights documentation must be timely obtained, negotiated, and executed. During the Interconnection Study process, GPC and Participant will discuss and agree upon Interconnection Facilities and Access Route siting. Participant also must coordinate with GPC to prepare to GPC’s satisfaction the property (e.g., grading and preparation of the ICF Site and suitable Access Route) and turn access to the property over to GPC by no later than one year before the projected transmission in-service date. After initial preparation of the Access Route, a Winning Bidder who enters into an Awarded Contract must also: (i) regarding Awarded Contracts that are PPAs, maintain, at its own expense, the Access Route in accordance with GPC’s standards and to GPC’s satisfaction throughout the PPA Term; and (ii) regarding Awarded Contracts that are APAs, validly transfer all real property rights required by GPC for access to and maintenance of the ICF Site and the Interconnection Facilities.
Notice to Proceed. Notice to proceed requirements for a winning Participant whose Facility will interconnect with GPC depend on the interconnection request/IA status when the Commission issues the Certification:
A Winning Bidder with an active IA (i.e., IA not in suspension) must submit a notice to proceed to initiate construction of Interconnection Facilities by the later of 14 Days after the Commission issues the Certification or the date dictated in the LGIA;
If winning Participant’s Facility is the subject of an IA in suspension, Participant must have requested to come out of suspension within seven Days after advancement to the Short List as described in Section 1.1.D (Timing and Notification of Initiating Interconnection Process (New Facility)); or
If the interconnection request is still in study phase or if not in suspension but the IA has not been finalized, then by no later than 45 Days after the IA is provided to Participant for execution, Participant must submit a notice to proceed to initiate construction of Interconnection Facilities. Depending upon when Participant initiates the interconnection process, Participant may be required to enter into an engineering and procurement agreement with GPC to assume cost responsibility and allow pre-construction activities, such as engineering work and procurement of long lead-time materials, to commence before execution of the IA. 
Additional Guidance for Facilities Interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission System.
POI. The POI refers to the point where the Facility connects to the Interconnection Provider’s Electric System. The POI is not necessarily the same as the point of change of ownership of equipment.
Sample Diagrams. The example diagrams below may assist Participant in determining where the POI could be located for its Facility. 
Additional Information. Information regarding interconnection to the Southern Company Transmission System may be found at Southern Company’s OASIS website at https://www.oasis.oati.com/SOCO. Information about Seller’s interconnection under the Southern OATT can be found in the Generator Interconnection folder on the Southern Company OASIS home page. A few examples of documentation include Interconnection Requirements for Inverter-Based Generation, Generator Interconnection Business Practices, and Inverter-Based Electric Storage Operating Policy. If Participant needs further clarification, please use the question-and-answer process available on the IE Website.

Interconnection of a non-ess Facility to the Electric System of an ITS Participant (>40 kV)
The following requirements apply to a Bid for a Non-ESS Facility interconnecting with the transmission system of an ITS Participant (GTC, MEAG Power, or Dalton) with the POI at greater than 40 kV.
Procedure Guidance. If the Facility will interconnect to a transmission facility owned by an ITS Participant, Bidder’s interconnection application and IA will be with the applicable ITS Participant. Each ITS Participant uses its own Interconnection Study process and Bidder is responsible for determining all rules, practices, policies, and timelines with which it must comply to obtain an Interconnection Agreement with the ITS Participant. If Bidder has not submitted an interconnection request as of the date the Bid advances to the Competitive Tier, Bidder must initiate the interconnection process with the appropriate Interconnection Provider at least seven Days before the Short List determination date stated in the Solicitation Schedule.
ESS Bid Interconnection Restrictions. If the Bid is for a Facility that includes an ESS, interconnection to an ITS Participant substation is not allowed.
Bidder Cost Responsibility. If Bidder’s Facility will interconnect with an ITS Participant, Bidder is responsible for all Interconnection Study-related costs, in addition to any interconnection costs and risks up to and beyond the POI associated with any ITS Participant (non-GPC)-owned transmission facilities. Interconnection costs generally include equipment such as the ITS Participant-owned interconnection substation, the GSU transformer (for conversion up to the interconnecting voltage level), Facility-side generator interrupting device, all Station Service equipment, tie-line (which carries electrical power and communications), and any additional equipment (such as a utility-owned interrupting device and metering needed to connect to the Interconnection Facilities), as well as any additional real property for the interconnection substation and access and any operation and maintenance expenses and administrative costs. In addition, if applicable, a Winning Bidder is responsible for the costs, risks, and coordination of Affected System Upgrades. It is Bidder’s responsibility to determine and review all information regarding interconnection costs.
Interconnection Impacts. Interconnection impacts to the Electric System are unique to the specific design and location of each Facility and may require new or modified equipment beyond the POI. If a Facility is interconnecting with an ITS Participant, GPC will not impute to the Bid any costs for any new or modified ITS Participant-owned or Affected System-owned transmission Interconnection Facilities beyond the POI. Those costs must be determined by Bidder and may be included in the Bid price. Any reimbursement for these costs is a matter strictly between the ITS Participant or Affected System and Bidder. However, any costs beyond the POI on the Southern Company Transmission System (i.e., one of the Southern Companies is an affected system to the Interconnection Provider) will be imputed to the Bid during the Bid evaluation and should not be included in the Bid price. In this circumstance, Seller must provide payment or security for design, procurement, and installation of the new or modified equipment beyond the POI on the Southern Company Transmission System according to the terms of an affected system construction agreement with the applicable Southern Company Transmission System owner. If the Facility achieves Commercial Operation or Closing occurs, as applicable, the security will be returned to Seller or repayment will be made according to the affected system construction agreement or the Southern OATT, as applicable. 
Delivery Impacts. For Bids advanced to the Competitive Tier, GPC will develop a cost estimate for Electric System improvements, if any, to the Southern Company Transmission System, the Georgia ITS, or any other Electric System necessary to deliver the energy from the POI to GPC’s customers. These costs will be imputed to the Bid when evaluating the economics of the Bid. 
Interconnection of a Non-ESS Facility Outside Both the Southern Company Transmission System and Georgia ITS (PPA Bidders Only)
The following requirements apply to a PPA Bid for a Facility that does not include an ESS and is not interconnecting directly to the Southern Company Transmission System or to the Georgia ITS.
Bidder Cost and Compliance Responsibility. Bidder is responsible for all costs and risks, including interconnection and delivery, and coordination necessary to transmit energy from the Facility to the selected Southern Transmission Interface, if necessary. These costs can include transmission and distribution costs, scheduling costs, generation and energy imbalance costs, congestion charges, operating reserve charges, and the costs of rights to use the Electric System. Each Bidder must procure Firm Transmission Service for the full output of the Facility to carry out delivery to the selected Southern Transmission Interface. Each Bid must identify the Southern Transmission Interface to which the Facility will deliver. Bidder is responsible for determining all transmission-related rules, practices, and policies with which it must comply for both interconnection and delivery to the selected Southern Transmission Interface.
Delivery to Southern Transmission Interface. GPC encourages each Bidder to begin any TSR process from the POI to the selected Southern Transmission Interface as early as possible. In any event, to procure the required Firm Transmission Service, Bidder must initiate the TSR process with the appropriate provider at least seven Days before the Short List determination date stated in the Solicitation Schedule. Bidder must describe in its Bid its ability to meet the RCOD or RCD, as applicable, based upon the applicable Firm Transmission Service process timeline for delivery to the selected Southern Transmission Interface.
Interface Information. A Southern Transmission Interface is defined as a point where the Southern Company Transmission System connects to a neighboring Transmission Service Provider and can receive Firm Transmission Service deliveries from the Transmission Service Provider. The Southern Transmission Interface has five primary interfaces: TVA, VACAR, Florida, MISO, and FPL-NW. The map below is not intended to indicate that the Georgia ITS, PowerSouth Energy Cooperative, or Crisp County, Georgia are included in the Southern Company Transmission System.


Imputed Costs. Although Bidder is responsible for all costs and risks to deliver to the selected Southern Transmission Interface, there may be additional costs to deliver from the selected Southern Transmission Interface to GPC’s customers. These costs should not be included in the Bid price. However, GPC will impute these costs to the Bid.
Interconnection Impacts. Interconnection costs for a Facility not interconnecting directly to the Southern Company Transmission System or to the Georgia ITS will not be imputed to the Bid during the Bid evaluation; all those costs and risks are Bidder’s responsibility and may be included in the Bid price. Any reimbursement for these costs is a matter strictly between the Electric System owner and Bidder. However, interconnection costs beyond the POI on the Southern Company Transmission System (i.e., one of the Southern Companies is an affected system to the Interconnection Provider), if any, will be imputed to the Bid during the Bid evaluation and should not be included in the Bid price. In this circumstance, Seller must provide payment or security for the new or modified equipment on the Southern Company Transmission System beyond the POI according to the terms of an affected system construction agreement that would be executed by Bidder and the applicable Southern Company Transmission System owner. If the Facility achieves Commercial Operation, the security will be returned to Seller or repayment will be made according to the affected system construction agreement or the Southern OATT, as applicable. 
Delivery Impacts. For Bids advanced to the Competitive Tier, GPC will develop a cost estimate for Electric System improvements, if any, to the Southern Company Transmission System, the Georgia ITS, or any other Electric System necessary to deliver the energy from the selected Southern Transmission Interface to GPC’s customers. These costs will be imputed to the Bid when evaluating the economics of the Bid.

Exhibit E – Bid Assignment Guidelines
Bid Assignment 
Overview. 
A Bid may only be assigned, including any assignment of a previously assigned Bid to the original Bidder, with the prior written notice to and consent of GPC in accordance with the requirements of this Exhibit E (Bid Assignment Guidelines).
For each proposed Bid Assignment, Bidder and the proposed Bid assignee named in and executing the Consent Request (“Bid Assignee”) must review the requirements of this Exhibit E (Bid Assignment Guidelines) and agree to the GPC Bid Assignment Consent Form included as Attachment 1 (GPC Bid Assignment Consent Form) to this Exhibit E (“Consent Request”).
These guidelines are limited to Bid assignments during the All-Source RFP Bid solicitation phase (each attempted or completed assignment, a “Bid Assignment”). For assignments, transfers, or other changes after Awarded Contract execution, the contracting party must comply with requirements in those agreements. For purposes of this Exhibit E (Bid Assignment Guidelines) a Change of Control of a Bidder will be deemed an assignment, subject to the provisions of this Exhibit E. For purposes of this Exhibit E, a “Change of Control” is any transaction or series of related transactions which, if consummated, would result in Bidder being an Affiliate of a different Ultimate Parent Entity immediately after the transaction or series of transactions. For purposes of this definition, the ”Ultimate Parent Entity” of a Person is the Person who: (i) directly or indirectly controls 50% or more of the outstanding capital stock or other equity interests in the Person; (ii) has ordinary voting power; and (iii) does not itself have an Ultimate Parent Entity.      
Notice and Consent Requirements.
Notice Requirements.
